text.text:
I recently visited this restaurant and had a rather mixed experience. We arrived around 8:50 AM on a Sunday without a prior reservation and ended up waiting for more than an hour. The restaurant follows a token system for managing crowds, which is quite organised. We received token number G-13, and at that time they were serving D-10. We finally got our table around 10:20 AM. However, there isn’t much waiting area available, so most of the time you have to stand outside.

The food was decent overall. I enjoyed the Masala Dosa, Sagu Masala Dose, Khara Bath, and Filter Coffee. The Wasa was average and slightly undercooked. The dosas were tasty but very oily, similar to the style at Rameshwaram, and quite heavy – one dosa was enough to fill me up.

This is probably a place to try just once for the experience. If you forget to reserve your seat, I suggest opting for a parcel instead of dining in. Parcel orders take about 10–15 minutes, and you can enjoy your meal at a nearby temple area or outside.

Overall, the restaurant is well-managed in terms of crowd but could improve on waiting comfort and making dishes a bit lighter.

text.text:
Vidyarthi Bhavan in Bangalore is one of the most iconic and famous places for dosa, and it truly lives up to its reputation in terms of popularity. The first thing to know before visiting is that it is always extremely crowded. You must first take a token, and even after that, the waiting time can easily be more than 30 to 40 minutes, especially during peak hours.

Coming to the food, the dosa was good and definitely worth the price. The masala dosa stood out more compared to the sagu masala dosa, with better flavor and overall satisfaction. I also tried the vada and kesari bath. The vada was decent and is served with sweet sambar, which is slightly different from the usual style. Kesari bath was tasty and well prepared. Tea, however, was quite normal and nothing special.

While the food is enjoyable, the hype around Vidyarthi Bhavan is very large, and expectations tend to go really high because of its fame. One thing I truly liked is how they have maintained the hotel in a very authentic way, preserving the old-time charm and traditional feel.

The place is always crowded, and there is no proper parking space, which can be inconvenient. Overall, it’s a good experience at least once for the food and nostalgia.

I visited Vidyarthi Bhavan on my own to finally experience this iconic place. I was prepared for a long wait, assuming I’d have to stand in line for an hour. To my surprise, the staff seated me with three others at a shared table, and I got a seat within just two minutes. That was such a pleasant surprise!

The shared table ended up being one of the highlights of my visit. The people I sat with were warm and friendly, and we had a lovely conversation. One gentleman told me he’d been coming here since 1965, and hearing his stories while watching him enjoy his meal made the experience even more special.

The place has an old-world charm that feels like stepping back in time. It carries a nostalgic atmosphere that’s hard to find these days.

I ordered the sagu dosa and a cup of coffee. The sagu was slightly on the spicy side for my taste, but everything else was just perfect. If you’re visiting Bengaluru, Vidyarthi Bhavan is as much about the experience and history as it is about the food.

I visited Byg Brewski Brewing Company with my friends on a weekend night to celebrate one of my friend's birthdays, and we had an amazing time. The place was lively and full of energy, which is expected since it's one of the most popular spots in Bangalore. It was quite crowded, so the service took a little longer than usual, but the overall experience easily made up for it.

The ambiance is one of the best parts of this place. We were seated next to the water body, which created a beautiful and relaxing atmosphere. There were a couple of ducks roaming around the property, which was a lovely surprise and added to the charm of the place. There was also a dance performance happening that evening, making the whole place feel vibrant and entertaining.

Coming to the food, everything we ordered was delicious. The pizzas, nachos, and drinks were all excellent and worth trying. But the real highlight of the meal was the Tres Leches dessert. It was absolutely amazing and easily one of the best desserts I've had. I would highly recommend saving room for it.

Overall, we had a memorable evening filled with good food, great music, a beautiful ambiance, and even a birthday celebration with cake. If you're looking for a lively place to hang out with friends or celebrate a special occasion, Byg Brewski is definitely worth visiting. Just be prepared for a bit of a wait if you're going on a busy weekend.

I used to be a regular customer here and always loved the vibe, but my experience during a team dinner yesterday was incredibly disappointing. The place has truly lost its charm, and the drop in quality is shocking.

The Food & Drinks

The Good: The Tres Leches was the only saving grace of the night—absolutely delicious.
The Bad: The rest of the food was a massive letdown. I was genuinely surprised by how off-balance and awful the flavors were.
The Drinks: The mocktails were overwhelmingly sweet, tasting more like pure sugar syrup than a crafted beverage.

Service & Execution
The Ugly: The service was painfully slow. We had to wait a full hour just for a simple serving of fried rice.

Ambience & Maintenance
The venue is showing serious signs of neglect. There was noticeable dust everywhere, and the seating has not been maintained well. The chairs were highly uncomfortable, making it hard to actually sit back and enjoy the evening.

I never expected this level of service and food quality from BYG. It’s disheartening to see a favorite spot slide this far down. They urgently need to look into their kitchen efficiency, recipe consistency, and basic housekeeping.

text.text:
The Ultimate Bengaluru Brewery Experience 🍻

Byg Brewsky (Hennur) definitely lives up to the hype as the most popular outlet in the city. If you’re looking for the quintessential "Bengaluru vibe," this is exactly where you’ll find it.

The atmosphere here is incredible—spacious, lively, and yet soothing with the right balance of light music. It’s easily one of the most happening spots in town, perfect for both a high-energy night out or a chill evening.

The Brews: Their in-house brewery is top-notch with a wide variety of craft beers and a full bar.

The Food: We explored a bit of everything—chicken, fish, pork, and roasted corn. Every dish was outstanding, featuring very rich, distinct flavors.

A Small Quibble: While the quality is high, the starters come with a lot of onions and boiled corn on the side, which feels a bit like "filler" given the premium pricing.

Booking is Essential: Don’t just show up! Prior booking is a must to ensure you get a table, especially since the weekend crowd is massive.

Price Point: It is on the higher side, but the ambiance and food quality make it worth the spend.

Verdict: A must-visit destination for anyone in Bengaluru. This review is based entirely on my personal experience.

text.text:
Byg Brewski on Sarjapur Road is not just a brewery, it’s an experience.
One of the biggest brewpubs in Bengaluru, this place feels like a mini holiday spot with massive open spaces, greenery all around, and that stunning waterfront seating that instantly sets the mood.
What made our visit extra fun was their “Spin to Win” activity – running daily from 12 PM to 8 PM.
Every table gets a spin, everyone wins something – no awkward rules, no pressure to finish food fast. Just spin mid-meal and enjoy the surprise. Such a cool concept!
Coming to the food – every dish we tried was on point.
The peanut fried wontons were super crunchy and addictive,
avocado tacos were fresh and flavourful,
pickle mushroom balls had a nice tangy kick,
and the paneer puffs were soft inside with a crispy outside.
For main course, the mushroom stroganoff was rich, creamy and super comforting.
Desserts were heavenly – the chocolate cake was pure indulgence and the raspberry chocolate mousse was light, balanced and delicious.
Drinks were equally good – refreshing watermelon mocktail, their in-house brewed beer, and a fun Byg shot to end it on a high.
Service was amazing – quick, friendly, and very attentive.
Overall, Byg Brewski Sarjapur Road is perfect for date nights, celebrations, or just a chill evening with great food, drinks, vibes and fun experiences.
Definitely a must-visit if you love breweries with a view.

I recently visited Byg Brewski Brewing Company on Sarjapur Road and overall had a really enjoyable time! The ambience is one of the biggest highlights — the vast, vibrant space with both indoor and outdoor seating creates a great vibe for a casual night out, dinner with friends, or even a relaxed date night. The poolside and garden-like seating areas made the evening feel extra special.

The craft beers and beverages are definitely worth trying, with several refreshing options on tap that pairs well with the food. The staff were attentive and friendly, and we felt well-looked after — they even suggested some good brews and dishes.
In terms of food, we had a mix — a few dishes were delicious and well-presented, while some felt more average in taste. But overall it paired nicely with the drinks and complemented the experience. Growing up in Bengaluru, I've visited CTR Malleshwaram many times. I recently went back after almost a decade, and I'm happy to say the taste hasn't changed at all. The hype is absolutely justified—the food is still delicious.

The masala dosa is outstanding, the goli bajjis are a must-try, and if you're a coffee lover, their filter coffee is among the best.

Personally, I felt the dosa had a bit too much butter/oil for my liking, but that's just my preference.

The service, however, could be better. The waiters are always in a rush, which can sometimes lead to confusion with orders, and they aren't always very polite while handling it.

Parking is another challenge, but that's something you'd expect in Malleshwaram.

Overall, despite a few minor drawbacks, CTR continues to be one of Bengaluru's iconic food destinations and is definitely worth a visit.

text.text:
Ambience (5/5)-
Situated in the heart of JP Nagar, Pump house has made a very big name for itself throughout the years. A huge nearly open environment with lots of plants, coolers and quirky spots for dining, this place offers a great tropical vibe at day and an entirely different vibe at sunset. My only feedback- the music can get a little too loud at times.

Food and drinks (5/5):
This being my second time, I have ordered a handful of vegetarian dishes and they're made and presented with utmost care. Paneer ghee roast was a delectable starter. Thai green curry was made with authentic sticky rice and is a must have. Their Kahlua soaked Tiramisu is a stand out in the dessert section. It's creamy, perfectly layered and not sweet enough to allow you to order it again.

Their beers have always been great. I've had the pleasure of trying their stout on a winter noon and their belgian wit on a hot summer noon and these are some of the best craft beers in the city, right there with the creme de la creme. Their mocktails, especially the ones that have a concoction of fruits are ideal picks for the sober folks.

Service (5/5)-
The staff greets you with a Namaste right from the entrance, the floor managers and bartender visited our table to make sure we're enjoying our food and drinks. Service was polite, timely, accommodating and quick, even on a fully packed holiday afternoon. Special mention to Dipak for very good service and for suggesting dishes we liked.

The only point of concern here are the prices but the experience very well makes up for it. This is a great place to plan your dates, casual outings with friends and family. I'd always recommend The Pump House to anyone who loves appetizing food and beer crafted to perfection.

text.text:
We initially decided to check out Communiti because it boasts close to 29,000 reviews online, and after our evening here, I completely understand why it has earned every single one of them! The hype is incredibly real. If you are looking for exceptional food and drinks on Residency Road, this place is an absolute must-visit.

We ended up ordering quite a feast for our table of three, and every single item exceeded our expectations. First off, they have an incredible craft beer deal: ₹1499 for 2 liters of beer plus a starter. We originally wanted the IPA, but since it was out, we went with the Wheat beer and were pleasantly surprised by how smooth and refreshing it was.

The cocktail menu is top-tier. My friend ordered a Bloody Mary and a Margarita and absolutely loved both. I tried a 'Mango Madness' mocktail, which was a complete yorker, absolutely delicious. We also gave the Tequila Sunrise a try, and it instantly became one of our table favorites!

For food, the portions are incredibly generous. We got the Home Made Nachos with Chicken Chunks, which was a massive serving, and the Butter Garlic Spicy Chicken was simply superb. We also ordered the Veg Club Sandwich (nice and juicy, though leaves a tiny bit of room for improvement) and the Bruschetta Chicken Penne, which my friend declared was some of the best pasta she’s ever had.

Yes, we ordered a lot, but when the food and drinks are this spectacular, who cares? My friend even said she hasn’t experienced food and drinks this good in a long time.
Highly recommend coming here with an empty stomach and good company!

Communiti is exactly the type of place to be on a Friday night out.

The long shared seating is perfect for big groups, the music is lively enough to keep the energy up without killing the conversation, and two pitchers in (Belgian Wheat and Ragi Gold Lager, both excellent) the night just took care of itself.

For the location and the overall experience, the prices are surprisingly affordable. Vibe, food, cost all solid. Definitely coming back.

text.text:
Visited Community for the first time on a Saturday night, and I honestly expected a much better vibe. The venue is split into two sections-the ground floor is Community, while the upper floors are a different restaurant that’s not even listed on Google Maps, which made the whole setup a bit confusing.

For a Saturday, the crowd was surprisingly sparse. I was expecting a lively young crowd, but it felt more like a family restaurant than a nightlife destination.

The food was just average, and the drinks didn’t stand out in any way. There’s nothing on the menu that would make me want to come back over the many other options in the city.

One thing that really spoiled the ambience was the odd disco light setup. It looked like a cheap black-box disco light constantly flashing, which felt completely out of place and took away from the overall atmosphere.

Overall, it wasn’t a bad experience, but it definitely didn’t live up to the hype. There are far better places in Bangalore if you’re looking for good food, creative drinks, and a lively weekend vibe.

Halli Mane located in the prime location of Malleswaram serves authentic South Indian dishes. It is a must visit place during their special mango and Jackfruit Mela.
We visited @ Mango mela when they served different mango items, Mango Festival Meal, served at ₹450, little expensive but dishes served were top notch.
As we entered, the most notable part was the service style, neither it was a buffet nor a normal setup of any standard Restaurant, the  service was like a Wedding feast - Dining in a row or Eating together in a traditional line at a function पंगतीत जेवणे. On the banana leaf the dishes were served in quick succession, repeatedly one after the other.
The food truly gives that authentic marriage food vibe, with a rich flavorful taste. Dosa, and the delicious mango themed meal served was awesome.
This restaurant is located in a very crowded area, somewhat difficult to find a parking place as only roadside parking is possible. When we reached we had to wait for half an hour as the restaurant was crowded and after we completed our meals the queue was much longer.
On the front of cleanliness they need to look into the basics and keep overall hygiene in place, provide better washroom
On the whole we had a wonderful experience and would definitely recommend this place to others for a traditional meal on banana leaf experience.
Visited 09.05.26

Visited the best biryani spot in Bangalore – and it truly lives up to the hype!

• The aroma itself makes you hungry!

• Chicken Biryani
• Paneer Biryani
• Gobi Manchurian
• Manchurian
• Tandoori Butter Roti
• Soft Drinks

• The biryani taste is excellent – one of the best in Bangalore.
• Perfect spice level and well-cooked meat.
• Mutton roast was flavorful and rich.
• Overall food quality is very good.

Ambience:
• Average – can be improved.

Service:
• Service is average.
• Order processing and response time could be better.

If you are craving biryani in Bangalore, this is the place to visit. In my opinion, Meghana serves one of the best biryanis in the city. 🍛🔥

Visited Nagarjuna after hearing a lot about it, and overall it lived up to the hype.

It’s located on the main road in a prime area, on the 1st floor, with a huge seating capacity. Even though it was quite crowded, we didn’t have to wait much for a table. The place is well-maintained, clean, and the staff were polite, well-mannered, and quick with service.

We tried their famous Andhra thali (₹350), which is unlimited. It included rice, dal, a dry sabzi (changes daily), chutneys (I think cucumber and coconut), sambar, rasam, curd, chaas, and a sweet (dalia). You can keep getting refills.

Taste-wise, everything was genuinely very good and flavorful. The only item I didn’t enjoy much was the rasam—it was extremely spicy and had a strong garam masala punch.

One thing I really liked was that the food didn’t feel overly oily or heavy, which is rare for thali places.

We also ordered Mushroom Sholay (₹330), which was quite tasty, and a Thums Up (₹70).

If not tried would recommend, especially for the thali experience.

Nagarjuna Restaurant in Marathahalli remains a top-tier destination for anyone craving authentic Andhra flavors. The star of the show is undoubtedly their legendary Andhra Meals—the combination of the aromatic ghee, spicy gunpowder (podi), and signature pappu is simply unbeatable and offers a true taste of tradition.

​The Chicken Nagarjuna and Sholay Kababs are consistently tender, well-marinated, and packed with a spicy punch that keeps you coming back for more. Despite the heavy crowds, the service is remarkably efficient and the staff manages the rush with a professional attitude. The restaurant maintains a clean, vibrant atmosphere that is perfect for a hearty family lunch or a quick office breakout. If you are in Marathahalli and looking for a high-quality, flavorful, and satisfying dining experience, Nagarjuna is a must-visit!

Quality seems to have dropped—or maybe competition’s just better now. This used to be a favorite, but my third visit after a long gap was disappointing. The 40 min long queue in heated conditions was not worth the hassle at all.

Al-Amanah Special Jumbo Roll:
This felt like a complete letdown for the price. The “special” tag was misleading—you only get a few bitter, burnt mushrooms, slices of boiled egg, and very average chicken. I expected a proper mix of toppings, but there was nothing of that sort.

Chicken Roast Jumbo Roll:
Tasted almost the same as the special roll. No distinct flavour minus the mushrooms & egg.

Crispy Chicken Roll:
The only good one—crispy, spicy, and actually flavourful.

Main Issue:
There’s a clear lack of flavour across the menu, often masked by excessive mayo and sauces which aren’t particularly flavourful to begin with. I love the fact they dont serve dry rolls which are an absolute pain but there is something missing big time here. Its not dry but where's the flavour. They really need better toppings, balanced seasoning, and elements like veggies, masala, or pickled additions to elevate the taste. Overall, it no longer hits the spot and isn’t worth the wait or hype. The chilled soft drinks was the best part about this visit.

Sad that one of my fav spots has come to this.

A Random Visit That Turned Into a Great Experience” ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐

My wife and I randomly decided to visit Karama without planning much, and honestly, it turned out to be a surprisingly great experience. From the moment we entered, the ambience felt warm and welcoming. The seating setup and overall vibe made the place feel premium yet comfortable.

The food was definitely the highlight of our visit. We tried a mix of dishes, and most of them were genuinely impressive. The mutton dishes especially stood out — soft, flavorful, and perfectly cooked. You can tell the kitchen knows how to handle non-veg items really well. Even the starters had good balance in seasoning and taste.

Service was another strong point. The staff was attentive, polite, and quick without being intrusive. It made the whole dining experience smooth and relaxed.

What I liked most is that despite hearing mixed reviews before visiting, our personal experience was actually very positive. Every restaurant can have off days, but on our visit, Karama delivered good food, nice ambience, and quality service.

If you enjoy flavorful non-veg food and want a good dine-in experience in Bengaluru, this place is definitely worth trying at least once with family or friends.

text.text:
I recently visited Sagar Restaurant and tried their special mango milkshake, which cost ₹170 including GST. The milkshake itself tasted good—fresh and enjoyable—but honestly, it didn’t feel special enough to justify the price.

For ₹170, I expected something more unique or premium in terms of taste or portion. While they did add a few mango pieces on top, it didn’t really make a big difference. I’ve had similar mango milkshakes at other places for much lower prices. In fact, just the other day I had a comparable drink elsewhere for around ₹60 (half portion), and it felt like much better value. With that comparison, this one feels clearly overpriced.

The place itself is decent. It’s fairly clean, and you can see they are making an effort to maintain hygiene, which is definitely a positive. The overall environment is okay, nothing particularly standout but comfortable enough.

That said, I personally feel the place is a bit overhyped, mainly because of the pricing not matching the experience. If the cost was more reasonable, it would have been a much better overall impression.

In short, good taste and clean setup, but pricing needs a reality check.

Sagar Restaurant is not just a place — it’s an emotion.
Man, I genuinely can’t have enough of this spot.
Let’s consider the facts.
It’s past midnight.
You’re hit with late-night cravings.
You’re dreaming of pav bhaji or jalebi fafda.
Entire Bangalore knows where you need to be.

Dabeli? On point.
Chaat? They’ve got it all.

Everything else? Absolute treat.
If you’re in Bangalore and craving proper street-style comfort food, especially late at night, Sagar Restaurant in Rajajinagar is the pilgrimage spot.

text.text:
Some places earn their popularity through clever marketing, while others earn it one plate at a time. This café undoubtedly belongs to the latter. It is perhaps the most talked-about café in Bengaluru, but the hype is entirely justified. From the very first bite, it becomes evident that this place is committed to authenticity rather than imitation.

The use of pure ghee elevates every dish, lending it an unmistakable richness and aroma that is difficult to find elsewhere. Unlike many cafés in Bengaluru that often imitate trends, presentation styles, or flavours, this establishment has created an identity of its own. The food is honest, traditional, and exceptionally satisfying.

The dose was outstanding, with the perfect balance of crispness and softness. Every bite reflected careful preparation and high-quality ingredients. Equally impressive was the idli sambar. The idlis were neither overly soft nor dense; they had the ideal texture to absorb the flavourful sambar beautifully, making every mouthful incredibly comforting and delicious.

A special mention goes to the filter coffee, which was nothing short of perfection. Rich, aromatic, and expertly brewed, it complemented the meal flawlessly and left a lasting impression. It is easily one of the finest cups of traditional filter coffee I have enjoyed in Bengaluru.

The consistency in taste, the authenticity of the preparation, and the evident focus on quality make this café stand apart from the rest. If you are a dosa enthusiast or simply appreciate genuine South Indian cuisine prepared with care, this place deserves to be at the very top of your list. It is a culinary experience that truly lives up to its remarkable reputation.

I recently visited The Rameshwaram Cafe, a bustling and highly popular spot known for its authentic South Indian flavors. The café is usually crowded, which clearly reflects its reputation for serving delicious dosas and idlis.
I ordered the Butter Benne Plain Dosa (₹120) along with a Masala Chai (₹40), with all prices inclusive of GST. The dosa was well-prepared with a rich buttery taste, and the chai had a pleasant, satisfying flavor that complemented the meal perfectly.
Due to the high demand, the waiting time for dosas can be slightly longer. However, the café has an organized system in place. There is a self-order token counter outside, which makes the ordering process easier. Once you get your token, you need to collect your food from designated counters—separate counters are assigned for dosas, idlis, juices, tea, and more. It is a fully self-service setup, but it is managed efficiently despite the crowd.
They also offer a variety of juices and desserts, adding more options for visitors.
Overall, a great place to enjoy authentic South Indian food with excellent taste. Be prepared for some waiting time, but the food makes it worth it. Highly recommended for dosa lovers.!

If you're looking for an authentic Bengaluru breakfast experience, Brahmins' Coffee Bar near Shankar Mutt Road is an absolute must-visit. This iconic eatery has earned its legendary reputation by serving a simple yet unforgettable menu that focuses on quality rather than variety. The soft, melt-in-your-mouth idlis paired with their signature coconut chutney are outstanding, while the crispy vadas are perfectly golden and packed with flavor. Their Khara Bath and Kesari Bath are equally delicious, and no visit is complete without enjoying a strong, frothy filter coffee that perfectly rounds off the meal.

The place has a charming old-world vibe and reflects the true essence of Bengaluru's traditional breakfast culture. Even though there is limited seating and parking, the constant crowd speaks volumes about its popularity and the consistency of its food. The service is incredibly quick, the prices are very reasonable, and everything is served fresh and hot.

What makes this place truly special is its commitment to maintaining the same authentic taste for decades. Whether you're a local or visiting Bengaluru for the first time, Brahmins' Coffee Bar offers a nostalgic culinary experience that you won't forget. Simple food, exceptional quality, and unmatched flavor make this one of the finest breakfast destinations in the city. Highly recommended!

text.text:
Hidden Gem: Old-School Sandwiches & Badam Milkshake Magic
Tucked away in a bustling corner that’s been slinging treats for decades, this no-frills joint is a time capsule of flavor. The faded signboard and worn wooden counters scream “vintage,” but don’t let the age fool you—the quality here shines brighter than ever. We’ve been coming back for years, and it never disappoints.
First bite: the sandwich. They grill it right in front of your eyes on a sizzling tawa, no shortcuts. Freshly sliced veggies—crisp onions, juicy tomatoes, shredded carrots—pile high with molten cheese and a secret green chutney that packs a tangy punch. The bread? Soft yet crusty, buttered to perfection. It’s messy, hearty, and hits that street-food sweet spot without feeling greasy. At under ₹80, it’s a steal for the portion size.
Then, the star: badam milkshake. Thick, frothy goodness blended live with real almonds, cardamom, and a generous scoop of vanilla ice cream. You watch the magic happen—nuts ground fresh, milk frothing up—no powders or shortcuts. It’s creamy, not overly sweet, with that nutty aroma lingering. Pairs perfectly with the sandwich for a quick, satisfying fix.
Spotless counters, friendly uncles who remember regulars, and zero fuss. In a world of flashy cafes, this old spot keeps it real: clean, transparent, top-notch quality. Perfect pitstop after a ride or work crunch. 5/5—worth the nostalgia trip!

Ever since I moved to Bengaluru, I've made it a weekend ritual to check out a different brewery every chance I get. After trying quite a few, Windmills is still the one I keep comparing everything else to.

If you're into craft beer, you'll notice the little things - the balance, the freshness, and how clean each brew tastes. That's what really stood out here. Every beer I tried felt well thought out rather than just another house brew.

The place itself is just as memorable. The live jazz in the background, relaxed ambience, and attentive service make it easy to spend an entire evening here. I didn't explore much of the food menu, but the fish dish I ordered was excellent and paired really well with the beer.

Definitely one of my favourite breweries in the city, and a place I'll keep coming back to.

text.text:
Tried visiting Chulha Chauki da Dhaba, Jayanagar after hearing so much hype everywhere, but honestly it felt like just another normal restaurant with fancy presentation and social media hype 😅. The ambience is definitely nice and the rooftop setup with lights gives a good vibe for photos and hanging out with friends 🌃✨, but when it comes to the actual food, it was pretty average and nowhere close to the level people describe online. The papad topping starter looked colorful and tempting, but taste-wise it was very basic. Paneer items were okay-ish, not bad but nothing memorable either 🫠. Rotis and naan were decent, but again for the amount they charge, you expect something much better. Most dishes felt heavily priced just because of the “dhaba theme” and crowd popularity.

The biggest issue is that this place is seriously overrated and overpriced for what it offers 💸. You end up paying premium prices for food that tastes very ordinary. The quantity also doesn’t justify the cost at all. Even the chutneys and sides felt average, and some dishes looked better than they actually tasted. Service was fine but the waiting time and crowd make it feel overhyped. It’s not a bad place, but definitely not worth all the craze people create around it. You can easily find many places in Bangalore serving tastier North Indian food at much better prices 😅. Overall, it’s good for one-time visit and ambience photos 📸, but if you’re going mainly for amazing food, this place may disappoint you. Food was just okay, not something worth spending so much money on 🙃🍽️

text.text:
Chulha Chauki Da Dhaba in Jayanagar is a nice option when you're craving North Indian comfort food without the typical fine-dining setup. The restaurant is located on the 5th floor, but there's a lift available, so reaching it isn't an issue.

I visited for lunch, and the place was relatively quiet when we arrived. However, as the afternoon progressed, more tables started filling up, which is usually a good sign. The interiors are designed around a traditional dhaba theme, with rustic décor and seating that tries to recreate the roadside Punjabi dhaba experience.

The menu is quite extensive and covers both vegetarian and non-vegetarian Punjabi dishes. From paneer gravies, dal makhani, and stuffed parathas to butter chicken, kebabs, and other North Indian classics, there's enough variety for mixed groups. Portions are generous and pair well with their assortment of breads.

One thing worth noting is that they do not serve alcohol, so it's more of a family restaurant than a pub-style North Indian place.

Service was pleasantly quick. Despite the restaurant gradually getting busier, our food arrived within 15–20 minutes, and the staff were attentive throughout the meal.

Overall, Chulha Chauki Da Dhaba delivers a good combination of Punjabi food, dhaba-style ambience, and efficient service. It's a solid choice in Jayanagar when you're looking for hearty North Indian food in a relaxed, family-friendly setting.

text.text:
Located right on the famous fruits and flower street alongside legends like Vidyarthi Bhavan and Namma SLN, Roti Ghar definitely managed to impress. Despite the heavy crowds, the experience was seamless.

The Food Breakdown:

* Starters: The Spanish Manchurian (3.7/5) was a unique highlight—creamy spinach base with fried veg balls, mushrooms, and paneer. A very different and tasty twist!

The Manchow Soup (2.5/5) was unfortunately a bit too watery for my liking.

* Chaats: The Palak Chaat (4/5) was the absolute winner! A perfect medley of sweet, tangy, and spicy with a satisfying crunch from the kaju and palak.

The Masala Puri (3.5/5) was solid and traditional, though the Bhel Puri (2/5) lacked the "wow" factor and proper masala balance.

* Main Course: We had Roti, Pudina Roti, and Paneer Laziz (3.9/5). The paneer was incredibly soft (Nandini paneer) and paired perfectly with the spicy, kaju-filled gravy. Everything felt very fresh.

Vibe & Service:
The service was lovely—quick and amicable despite the place being jam-packed. They have a standing self-service area on the ground floor and a more relaxed AC seating area on the first floor. Also I loved the fact that they mentioned their main source like for paneer they use fresh nandini one after the fake paneer rampant in India and rotis are clearly distinguished between maida and whole wheat. Also super reasonable price for the quality and taste!

Total Verdict: A great spot for a variety of flavors if you are in the area. Don't miss that Palak Chaat!

Vapour Brewpub and Diner – Sarjapur Road is a perfect hangout spot for those who love great food, refreshing drinks, and a lively party vibe. Located on one of the busiest stretches of the city, this place surprisingly feels like a peaceful escape once you step inside, making it ideal for party lovers and weekend chill scenes.

The rooftop seating is one of the biggest highlights of this brewpub. Especially if you grab a corner-side table, the views are absolutely amazing. The open-air setup, combined with ambient lighting and a vibrant crowd, creates a fantastic atmosphere for both casual evenings and energetic nights. Whether you’re catching up with friends or planning a celebration, the rooftop adds a premium touch to the entire experience.

When it comes to food, Vapour doesn’t disappoint. The menu offers a good variety of options catering to different tastes, and the quality is consistently impressive. Alongside that, the selection of beverages, including a wide range of alcoholic drinks, is well-curated. From classic choices to signature brews, there’s something for everyone to enjoy.

Despite being located on a crowded and busy road, the vibe inside feels completely different—almost like stepping into a party zone away from the chaos outside. The music, crowd energy, and overall ambiance make it a favorite spot for party enthusiasts.

Service is decent, and the staff handles the rush efficiently, especially during peak hours. Overall, Vapour Brewpub and Diner offers a complete package of great views, tasty food, good drinks, and a lively atmosphere, making it a must-visit place on Sarjapur Road.

​We also tried the Pork Back Ribs, and honestly, words fall short. They were top-class! The meat was cooked to absolute perfection, and the rich BBQ sauce infused it with incredible flavor. Meat lovers, this is your paradise—do not miss out on this.
​Amazing music, stellar service and mouth-watering food. We will definitely be back for more!

Had a fantastic breakfast experience at Rameshwaram Cafe! The food was fresh, flavorful, and served with the authentic South Indian taste that the cafe is known for.

We tried a variety of dishes, including the Ghee Pudi Dosa, Pudina Roasted Dosa, Lemon Rice, Pulihora (Tamarind Rice), and Gongura Rice, along with their signature coffee. Every dish had its own unique flavor and was prepared perfectly.

The Ghee Pudi Dosa was the standout item crispy, aromatic, generously coated with ghee and podi, and absolutely delicious. The Pudina Roasted Dosa had a refreshing mint flavor and a wonderful crunch. The Lemon Rice was light, tangy, and comforting, while the Pulihora delivered the perfect balance of tamarind and spices. The Gongura Rice was packed with authentic Andhra flavors and was a treat for anyone who enjoys a slightly tangy and spicy rice dish.

The chutneys complemented every dish beautifully, and the portions were satisfying. To finish, we had their famous filter coffee, which was rich, aromatic, and the perfect end to the meal.

Highlights of the visit:

- Ghee Pudi Dosa – an absolute must-try
- Authentic South Indian flavors
- Freshly prepared food with quality ingredients
- Excellent variety of rice dishes
- Delicious filter coffee
- Quick service and energetic atmosphere
- Great presentation served on banana leaves

If you're a fan of South Indian cuisine, Rameshwaram Cafe is definitely worth visiting. The combination of flavorful dosas, delicious rice varieties, and excellent coffee makes it a place you'll want to come back to again and again!

text.text:
Ambience (4/5):
At the crossroads between Vittal Mallaya Road and Lavelle road, The Biere Club offers a very classy place to enjoy pint or two. It offers a rusty old Irish pub vibe with comfortable seating and games like snooker (on the first floor). The sound of the music is quite bearable.

Food and Drinks (3/5):
The 3 dishes I tried (2 veg starters and a dessert). Thai corn fritters and the Hummus dish were decent light accompaniments with beer although you'd expect much more in terms of taste and complexity for the prices you're paying. The Biere Club special sundae was nothing more than a basic ice cream you get on the street for about Rs 150 although they charge 3X of that.

Their beer quality, body and mouthfeel is definitely above average but their seasonal Mango Ale was worth a try. What disappointed is the lack of cocktails available here. There's a lot of hard liquor menu items but not a lot of cocktails. On the off chance someone like me is in the mood for an espresso martini, I had to give them the recipe to make it although it was done as per instructions.

Service (5/5):
Swain was great at suggesting, making conversation and even taking feedback positively too. The service in general was agile and courteous.

My only gripe with this place is being situated in one of the most expensive areas in Bangalore, the prices you'll pay will be exorbitantly high. I dined alone but the amount in the bill is usually what I see when I go out with a +1. So if price is a very decisive factor for picking the place, you might want to reconsider.

text.text:
SLV Corner is one of those classic spots that truly lives up to its reputation. Located very close to Ramakrishna Ashrama, it’s easy to find and a go-to for anyone craving authentic vegetarian food. Parking is fairly convenient for two-wheelers right in front, while four-wheeler parking can be a bit tricky with mostly street-side options.

The restaurant operates in two formats—a self-service section and a separate service restaurant just opposite. The self-service area mainly focuses on South Indian staples and chaats, while the service section offers a more extensive menu including North Indian and Chinese dishes. The ambience is simple and old-school, but clean and well-maintained, which adds to its charm.

Coming to the food, the self-service section delivers consistently great flavors. The masala puri, sev puri, idli with sambar dip, and masala dosa were all excellent and packed with authentic taste. The rava idli was soft and enjoyable, though the Bombay sagu could have been better. Their filter coffee was a solid finish—strong and satisfying. The garlic bread and pizzas may not be the focus here, but their traditional items truly shine.

The place is moderately priced, accepts both cash and UPI, and the service is quick with friendly staff, even during busy hours. It does get crowded, especially during peak times, but the fast turnaround keeps things moving.

Overall, it’s an iconic vegetarian spot in Basavanagudi, perfect for a quick bite or a wholesome meal. With hygienic food, generous thalis, and consistent quality, it’s definitely a place you’ll want to revisit and recommend.

Met an old friend here for drinks and dinner, and while the place had a few positives, the overall experience was fairly average.

Pros:

1. The staff were courteous, polite, and helpful throughout our visit.
2. The ambience had a rustic charm with an old-school sports pub vibe. The place was also clean and well maintained.
3. The restaurant is spread across three floors with ample seating space suitable for groups of all sizes.
4. We didn’t have to wait for a table, which was a plus.

Cons:

1. The elevator was extremely slow and quite small — it could barely accommodate three adults comfortably.
2. Service was disappointingly slow. We waited nearly 30 minutes for the beer tasters, only to find that many of the craft beers were unavailable. Also, they don’t brew their own beers and instead source them from Toit.
3. The food was average overall and slightly too spicy for our liking.

Visited The Reservoir for the first time after loving the Indiranagar branch for a long time, and this branch also impressed us with the food, ambience, and service.

The peri-peri french fries were really good — crispy, well-seasoned, and served in a good quantity.

We also tried the veg Thai baos. The flavors were excellent with a nice balance of tanginess and crunch, but the stuffing was a little too oily. Apart from that, the taste was really good and I would definitely order it again, probably requesting less oil next time.

The Thai green curry with jasmine rice was easily the highlight for me, just like in the Indiranagar branch. The curry had a rich coconut flavor, the vegetables were cooked perfectly, and the portion size was very satisfying.

The ambience was cosy and pleasant, though the music felt slightly loud. Service was quick and friendly, and the pricing is actually very reasonable for the quality and ambience they offer.

Overall, a really good experience and definitely a place we would visit again.

text.text:
We recently decided to try sweets in Bengaluru and chose Anand Sweets, Sarjapur for our first experience. Unfortunately, it turned out to be quite disappointing.

Before purchasing, I wanted to taste a Gulab Jamun, which is a fairly common practice in many sweet shops. I politely requested the counter staff if I could try one piece before buying. Even after clearly stating that I was willing to pay for the sample, the request was repeatedly declined without any explanation. It wasn't about getting something for free—it was about understanding the quality before making a purchase.

The interaction itself left a poor impression. Customer service is not just about selling products; it's about helping customers make informed choices. The way the request was handled felt dismissive and unwelcoming.

Because of this experience, I decided to reduce my purchase and bought only half a kilogram instead of the larger quantity I had originally planned. Unfortunately, after reaching home and trying the Gulab Jamun, the product did not meet expectations either. The texture, taste, and overall quality were far below what I would expect from a premium sweet brand. In fact, it was among the least enjoyable Gulab Jamuns I have had in recent years.

One thing Anand Sweets does exceptionally well is presentation. The packaging is attractive, premium-looking, and well-designed. However, good packaging can only create a first impression; ultimately, it is the quality of the sweets that customers remember.

My honest takeaway from this visit is that the brand appears to invest heavily in presentation and packaging, but the product quality and customer experience did not justify the reputation or premium pricing.

For people who genuinely love traditional Indian sweets and prioritize taste, this outlet may not meet expectations. And for those considering gifting sweets, while the packaging looks impressive, the quality of the sweets inside should be the deciding factor.

I recently visited this place in HSR and overall it was a really good experience. The ambience is very nice, peaceful, and well maintained. It feels comfortable the moment you walk in and does not feel too loud or rushed, which I personally liked.

The people working here are genuinely good and polite. I was served by Krishna and Reema, and they did a wonderful job. They were attentive, respectful, and made sure we were comfortable throughout our time there. Their service definitely made the experience better.

There was one incident where I was served chicken even though I am a pure vegetarian. I noticed it immediately and did not eat it. Yes, it was a mistake, but I am not reviewing them negatively for that. As humans, we all make mistakes sometimes. We never know what someone might be dealing with on a given day, and these things can happen. What matters is how the rest of the experience is, and that was mostly positive.

Coming to the food, they actually have very good vegetarian options. The vegetarian food we tried was tasty and well prepared. One honest feedback would be about the paneer ghee roast. I personally did not like it much as it felt very plain and the only thing noticeable was excess ghee without much flavour. Apart from that, the other vegetarian dishes were enjoyable.

They also have a separate smoking zone, which is thoughtfully planned and does not disturb others. We visited with a small kid, and the place felt quite kid friendly. It was not overly crowded, which made it comfortable for families as well.

Parking is also not a problem since you can find space nearby on the road, which is convenient.

Overall, it is a nice place with good ambience, kind people, and decent food options. I would definitely consider visiting again. That is why I am giving it 4 out of 5 stars.

text.text:
We visited this restaurant for lunch on a weekday expecting a relaxed dining experience, but unfortunately the service turned out to be quite disappointing. Although we were informed over the phone that reservations were not required, we still had to wait around 5–10 minutes to get a table after arriving. That part was manageable.

The biggest issue during our visit was the extremely slow service. Several food items at the buffet counters were left empty for long periods and were only refilled after repeatedly informing the staff. We even had to wait over 15 minutes just to get rotis, which became frustrating after a point. The serving staff did not appear very attentive, and the coordination overall seemed lacking.

That said, one person who truly stood out was the manager, an elderly gentleman who handled the situation with sincerity and professionalism. He personally monitored the counters, checked on guests, and genuinely tried his best to ensure food was refilled quickly. His attitude and effort were definitely appreciated and probably the most positive part of the experience.

The ambience of the restaurant was average overall. While the dining area was decent, the restrooms were not maintained properly during our visit. When this was brought up, the staff mentioned that maintenance work was ongoing.

The restaurant offers a large variety of vegetarian dishes, which initially creates a good impression. However, when it comes to taste, most of the food felt quite mediocre and did not really justify the pricing. Nothing tasted particularly bad, but very few dishes stood out enough to be memorable.

Overall, the place has potential because of its wide menu and courteous manager, but the slow service, average food quality, and lack of proper management made the experience underwhelming.

Exceptional Main Course: The Paneer Tikka, Paneer Gravy, and Gobi Manchurian were standout dishes, alongside a well-prepared Veg Fried Rice.

​Dynamic Open Kitchen: The open kitchen concept added a great visual element, allowing guests to watch the fresh preparation of dishes as they were being replenished.

​Attentive Service: The staff was proactive, particularly the server ensuring a constant supply of hot, fresh Naan at the table.
​Generous Add-ons: The menu included great "extras" like unlimited vanilla ice cream, Jaljeera, and a hearty, thick soup.
​Student-Friendly Pricing: A significant perk was the 15% student discount, making it a budget-friendly option for those with a valid ID.

​Dessert Inconsistencies: The experience was slightly let down by the sweets; the Gulab Jamun was served cold and the Halwa lacked sufficient sweetness.

​Crowded Atmosphere: Visiting around 7:00 PM resulted in a heavy rush, highlighting a lack of adequate seating and a cramped environment.

​Ventilation Issues: The layout is somewhat flawed, as most seats do not receive direct AC airflow, which can get uncomfortable during peak hours.

This place turned out to be a cracking find for a relaxed lunch with a bit of flair. We chose an outside table, which made the whole experience feel breezy and laid-back, with just the right amount of buzz around. It’s the kind of spot where you can enjoy a long conversation, catch a match on the screens, or simply soak in the lively atmosphere.

The food and drinks were a real highlight. We tried hummus with pita, alio olio, tiramisu, and a couple of mocktails - guava mary and passion fruit - and everything arrived beautifully presented and packed with flavour. Nothing felt rushed or careless; there’s real attention to what comes out of the kitchen.

What truly lifted the experience was the staff - warm, attentive, and genuinely keen to make sure we were having a good time. The menu covers a wide mix of cuisines, so there’s something for everyone.

One smart tip: pre-book through apps like Zomato - you can get discounts up to 40%, which makes the experience even sweeter.

Yes, it’s slightly premium on portions, but the quality, ambience, and service make it well worth it. A top spot in Whitefield for a relaxed meal or a casual celebration. 🍹🍝

Disappointing Dining Experience

This place doesn't feel like a proper restaurant—it’s more of a temporary setup, like a small function hall. The rooftop has been converted into a dining space, but it lacks ambiance and feels makeshift.

The service was rushed and impersonal, resembling a typical wedding food line. Staff hurriedly placed the banana leaf and began serving, without courtesy or attention. A meal priced at ₹180 doesn’t even include a water bottle—when requested, they insisted on payment first, in a rude manner.

There were no tissue papers to wipe the leaf, and the variety of dishes was minimal. Worse, not all listed items were served unless you kept track and reminded the staff.

The dining setup is a long table with chairs, more like a marriage hall than a restaurant. The staircase leading to the rooftop was narrow and unclean, adding to the discomfort.

Though the food tasted good, the limited variety and poor service do not justify the cost. There are better places in the city offering banana leaf meals with far superior service and value.

If you are looking for a spot that hits the trifecta of fantastic craft beer, delicious food, and top-tier hospitality—all without making your wallet cry—this is the place to be.

Here is why this brewery has officially become my go-to spot:

* The Brews: Smooth, distinct, and perfectly crafted. Whether you are into a crisp, refreshing wheat beer or a bold, flavorful stout, they’ve got something on tap for every palate.

* The Grub: Usually, brewery food is an afterthought, but the kitchen here deserves its own award. Every dish we ordered was fresh, bursting with flavor, and perfectly portioned.

* The Vibe & Service: This is what truly sets them apart. The staff treats you like family from the moment you walk in. The hospitality is warm, attentive, and genuinely welcoming without feeling intrusive.

* The Price Point: Honestly, given the premium quality of the food and drinks, the bill was a incredibly pleasant surprise. It’s rare to find high-end execution at such a reasonable, pocket-friendly price.

The Verdict: 10/10. Incredible value for money, an amazing atmosphere, and an all-around stellar experience. I’ll definitely be back (probably next weekend)!
Special mention of Shubham, Shailesh and Santosh for delivering fantastic hospitality.

If you are a fan of authentic grilled flavors and non-vegetarian delicacies in Bengaluru, Kabab Magic is a place you simply cannot ignore. I recently visited this outlet, and the experience was quite memorable. The restaurant is famous for its legendary grilled chicken and shawarma, and after tasting them, I can understand why. The meat was perfectly marinated, tender on the inside, and had that signature smoky char on the outside that defines a great kabab.
The menu is quite diverse, offering everything from classic Tandoori items to Chinese starters and flavorful Biryanis. Their Shawarma is definitely one of the highlights—well-stuffed and seasoned perfectly. The service was fairly quick despite the heavy evening rush, which shows they are well-managed. The seating area is decent, though it can get quite crowded during peak hours, especially on weekends.

I visited Taj Hotel in Shivajinagar after watching Instagram reels and seeing all the hype around their famous mutton biryani. Unfortunately, my experience was disappointing.
The building feels very old and the overall cleanliness was not up to the mark. The dining area did not look well-maintained, which affected the overall experience.
I ordered the mutton biryani expecting a rich and flavorful dish, but what I received was more like plain kushka with only two very small pieces of mutton. For a price of ₹380, the quantity and quality were far below expectations. The taste was just average and nothing special compared to many other biryani places in Bangalore.
The restaurant is well known and has a long history in Shivajinagar, which is one reason many people visit it.  However, based on my visit, the food did not justify the price. I felt that I paid a premium amount but did not receive a premium dining experience.Got Mutton biriyani in normal steel plate I don't think it's a MB.
Overall, I found the place overrated. Poor cleanliness, average taste, very little mutton in the biryani, and high pricing made this a disappointing visit. I would not recommend it to anyone looking for value for money

We recently tried the new à la carte menu at Sattvam and it was truly an elevated vegetarian dining experience. The ambience is beautiful with Bhagavad Gita wall art, ISKCON-inspired decor, and soothing Hare Krishna music that creates a calm and spiritual vibe.

What makes this place unique is their satvik cuisine — completely vegetarian with no onion and no garlic, yet every dish is packed with flavour and creativity.

Some highlights from our meal were the Peacock (crispy kattaifi nest with spicy potato mash), Smoked Sweet Corn Essence soup, Thai Mango Guava Mélange, Cheriya mini appam with coconut relish, Betel Leaf Tartare, Fried Dumplings, Golden Paneer Symphony, Signature Naanza, and the Butterfly Rice Bowl with sweet chilli basil stir fry. Every dish was beautifully presented and tasted excellent.

We ended with Basant, their take on kunafa with kataifi crisps and pista — a perfect dessert to finish the meal. The service was amazing throughout the experience.

They’re also known for their 70+ dish satvik buffet, making it a great place for anyone looking for a wholesome and premium vegetarian dining experience. Highly recommended.

text.text:
I really wanted to love Glen’s Bakehouse in Whitefield because the ambience is absolutely amazing—it’s easily one of the prettiest spots in the area. But unfortunately, the experience was a letdown.

The Good:
The food itself is decent. Their mini cupcakes are actually quite good—dense, flavorful, and exactly what you’d expect from a high-end bakery. The Red Velvet and Belgian Chocolate minis were tasty, but that’s where the positives end.

The Service (or lack thereof):
The service was horrible. We sat there for ages and no one bothered to check on us. Even when you go up to the counter, there’s hardly anyone there to assist you. You literally have to force yourself on the staff just to get an order in. For a place that charges a bomb price, you’d expect at least a basic level of hospitality, but the staff seemed completely indifferent and "least bothered."

The Biggest Issue:
My biggest complaint is the shocking lack of eggless or veg options. In a city like Bangalore, not having a solid range of eggless cupcakes (like a simple Eggless Red Velvet or Truffle) is a huge oversight. When I asked about it, the staff couldn't have cared less.

Verdict:
You’re paying a premium for the setting, but the service and the menu variety (especially for vegetarians/eggless eaters) just don't justify the cost. Unless you’re just there for a photo op, it’s hard to recommend.

text.text:
District 6, Rajajinagar is not just a brewery—it carries a legacy of crafting some of the finest brews in the city, paired with an ambience that perfectly blends industrial charm with a lively, premium vibe. Easily one of the best German-style microbreweries around.

This mango season, their special menu truly stands out. We tried the mango paneer chilli—unique and flavourful—and paired it with their seasonal mango-based beer, which was refreshing and well-balanced. The mango and watermelon mocktails were equally impressive.

For starters, the cheese dumplings and mushroom chilli were delicious. The main course with Thai curry & jasmine rice, along with phulka, veg curry, and paneer curry, was wholesome and satisfying. We ended on a perfect note with the chocolate fondant cake served with ice cream—rich, warm, and indulgent.

Overall, a must-visit for great brews, seasonal specials, and a complete dining experience.

If you're in Bangalore, Warrier Bakery is definitely worth a visit for its traditional bakery items and timeless flavors. And don't forget to carry your own bag while shopping!

Hello Google users,

I visited this place for their lunch buffet. It was an excellent experience with a great ambience and friendly staff.

They served a plate of crispy Nachos as the first dish. There were many starters which included Crispy Corn Salt & Pepper, Cheesy Mushroom Fingers, Crispy Veg in Hot Garlic Sauce, Peri Peri French Fries, Paneer Supreme Pizza, Vegetable Patty Burger and Vegetable Sandwich. All starters were fresh and tasty but the best starters were the Cheesy Mushroom Fingers and Crispy Veg in Hot Garlic Sauce.

For Grill options they served BBQ Grilled Paneer Tikka, BBQ Grilled Mushroom and BBQ Chatpata Pineapple. The BBQ Grilled Mushroom was the best as it was prepared to perfection and tasty delightful.

They had many options for Main dishes but we had only the Kashmir-e-Pulao with Raita. The Pulao was excellent as it had vegetables, cashew and raisins.

The dessert bar was stacked very well and they had 4 different ice cream flavours. There was a separate section for Gulab Jamun and Moong Dal Halwa. They had a lot of pastries and sweets and all of them were tasting good.

If you are in and around Sarjapur area in Bangalore then this place is a must visit for lunch or dinner with your family

Regards,
Deepak.

text.text:
We recently dropped by Olive Street Food Cafe in BTM Layout and came away really happy with the experience. In a busy area like BTM, where quick, tasty, and pocket-friendly options are always in demand, this place hits the sweet spot for casual street-style eats. It’s part of a small chain that’s gaining popularity for its value-for-money offerings.

Ambience & Vibe
The cafe has a bright, colourful, and youthful vibe with decent seating space — perfect for a relaxed meal with friends or family. It feels lively and energetic without being overly noisy during regular hours. The setup is simple yet inviting, making it a comfortable spot for hanging out over food and drinks.

Food We Tried & Taste
We ordered a mix of burgers, sandwiches, shakes, and a dry fruit salad. Honestly, the taste was awesome across the board!
•  The burgers and sandwiches were flavour-packed, fresh, and satisfying — proper street food soul with the right spices and crunch.
•  The shakes were thick, creamy, and refreshing — a perfect companion on a warm Bangalore day.
•  The dry fruit salad felt light, healthy, and surprisingly well-balanced.
Everything tasted homemade and generous in portion size. Nothing felt overly greasy or bland — they clearly put care into the flavours. For street food lovers, this is the kind of place that delivers comfort and satisfaction without fancy pretensions.

Pricing – Truly Affordable
One of the biggest highlights is the very normal and affordable pricing. You can enjoy a fulfilling meal here without burning a hole in your pocket. Most items are budget-friendly (many options under ₹150), making it ideal for students, young professionals, or families looking for value. The quality you get for the price is genuinely impressive.

Crowd & Timing – A Practical Note
This place is very crowded on weekends, so expect some waiting time and a lively, packed atmosphere. If you prefer a more relaxed experience, weekdays are much better — comfortable seating and quicker service. Pro tip: Visit during non-peak hours (early evening or mid-week) to enjoy it fully.

Overall Experience
Olive Street Food Cafe delivers exactly what it promises — tasty, hearty street food favourites at reasonable rates in a casual setting. It’s not fine dining, but it excels at being a reliable, feel-good spot for quick bites or relaxed meals. The combination of awesome taste, generous portions, and affordability makes it a strong contender in BTM’s food scene.

Final Verdict: Recommended for Budget Foodies

If you’re in BTM Layout and craving burgers, sandwiches, shakes, rolls, or light snacks at honest prices, Olive Street Food Cafe is worth a visit. It’s especially great for students, office-goers, or anyone who wants delicious food without the premium markup. Just plan your timing around the weekend rush!
We’ll definitely go back for more — particularly on a calm weekday. Keep up the good work, team! Highly recommended for casual, tasty, and wallet-friendly outings. 🍔🥪.

Special thanks to Kabir and Anil for their service for this trip. We will be back, hopefully, soon.

text.text:
Brahma Brews has a really nice ambiance with a relaxed, chill vibe that's perfect for spending an evening with family or friends. The overall atmosphere, seating, and setup are definitely the highlights of the place and are the main reason for my 4-star rating.

That said, there were a few areas that could use improvement. The service was quite slow—we had to wait around 35–40 minutes for our second starter to arrive, which affected the overall experience.

We also tried the Ananas and Mango beers, but unfortunately, the expected fruit flavors were barely noticeable. They tasted quite similar to regular beer, and the unique flavors didn't really come through.

The food was average at best. One of the chicken dishes appeared partially cooked and was served cold. More concerning was that both my son and I experienced stomach discomfort the following morning after our visit. While it's difficult to say with certainty what caused it, the experience left us a bit concerned.

Overall, Brahma Brews is a great place for its ambiance and laid-back atmosphere, but the food quality, flavor consistency, and service speed need improvement to match the excellent setting.

text.text:
If you’re scouting for a spot that looks like a million bucks on your Instagram feed, Jetlag in Rajajinagar is hard to beat. While the culinary side of things might not take off as smoothly as the name suggests, the atmosphere definitely reaches cruising altitude.

Here is the lowdown on why you should—and shouldn't—book a table here.

🌃 The View: A Total Showstopper
Let’s be honest: you come here for the skyline. Jetlag offers a spectacular view of the World Trade Center (WTC) and the Orion Mall area.
* The Vibe: When the sun goes down and the city lights flicker on, the place transforms. It is incredibly pretty at night and arguably one of the best spots in West Bangalore for a photoshoot.

* Photo Op: If you’re a fan of urban aesthetics, the backdrop of the illuminated WTC is worth the trip alone.

🤝 The Service: Top-Flight Staff
One area where Jetlag truly excels is the hospitality. The staff is great—attentive, professional, and they clearly do their best to manage the rooftop rush. In a city where service can sometimes be hit-or-miss, the team here keeps things grounded and friendly.

🍽️ The Food & Drinks: A Bit of Turbulence
This is where the experience becomes a bit "middle of the road."

* The Food: To put it simply, it was just okay. It’s standard pub/lounge fare that fills the stomach but doesn't necessarily leave you craving a second helping. It lacks that "wow" factor you might expect from such a high-end-looking venue.

* The Mocktails: For those of us sticking to the non-alcoholic side of the menu, be warned: they are incredibly sweet. It felt like the sugar levels were turned up to the max, which can be a bit much if you’re looking for a refreshing, balanced drink.

📍 The Verdict
Jetlag is a "view-first" destination. It’s the perfect place for a sundowner or a late-night hangout where the conversation and the scenery are the main events.
* Ambience: 4/5 (Great night views)
* Photography: 4/5 (Bring your best camera)
* Staff: 4/5 (Super helpful and welcoming)
* Food & Drink: 2.5/5 (Needs more balance and flavor atleast on the vegetarian side)

Restaurants must maintain basic cleanliness and proper kitchen hygiene to ensure food safety. I strongly hope the management takes this seriously and improves their standards so that no other customer faces such an experience.
Very disappointed.

I had a wonderful dining experience at 1522. The food was absolutely scrumptious, with an impressive variety on the menu. For starters, we tried the Paneer Manchurian, Dragon Baby Corn, Anjali Tava Fry, and the White Horse Special Chicken, all of which were flavorful and well-prepared.

For the main course, we ordered the Veg Dum Biryani and Chicken Donne Biryani. While the Veg Dum Biryani was initially slightly under-seasoned, it tasted excellent after adding salt, and the overall quality of the dish was very good. The Chicken Donne Biryani stood out with its authentic flavor.

We also enjoyed a selection of mocktails, including Spicy Chilli Guava, Pacific Blue, and Cinderella, which were refreshing and well-balanced.

The service was quick and efficient, and the cozy ambience added to the overall pleasant experience. Valet parking is available, which is convenient. Overall, it was a satisfying visit, and I would definitely like to dine here again.

text.text:
Had a wonderful dining experience at Neemsi and absolutely loved the philosophy behind the restaurant. One of the things that stood out is their commitment to purity—they source their spices directly from farmers, ensuring authentic flavours in every dish.
It's an all-vegetarian, no-alcohol restaurant that's redefining vegetarian dining with incredibly flavourful and thoughtfully crafted dishes.
We visited to try their newly launched Monsoon Edit, a seasonal menu that celebrates the flavours of the rainy season. Some of my favourites from the menu were the Chana Masala & Aloo Tikki Chaat, Mozzarella Veg Lollies served with Som Tam Salad, Mushroom Stroganoff Toast with Feta Cream, and the Teriyaki Vegetable Dimsums. For the mains, the Bhuna Sabz with Pyaaz & Nariyal Curry paired beautifully with the Basil Naan, while the Ravioli was another standout.
We ended the meal with Pisand Goreng and Neemsi's signature Mysore Pak Cheesecake, which was easily one of the highlights of the entire experience.
I also loved how Neemsi follows a seasonal menu concept called the Neemsi Edit, allowing guests to experience fresh, seasonal ingredients throughout the year. Thoughtfully curated dishes, beautiful presentation, and flavours that stay true to their philosophy make this a place worth visiting for a unique vegetarian dining experience.

Overall, the food definitely lived up to expectations.

A suprise restaurant on the 13th floor (sic). It is a covered terrace deck that gives an unrestricted view of famous buildings in Bangalore.

I past part of a very large group for lunch, celebrating the baptism of twin sisters. First off, the staff is par excellence. All of them were attentive, courteous, patient and went out of their way to make all of us feel special. The restaurant's appetizers were original preparations and scrumptious.
Lunch was Thai cuisine, and the chef certainly knows Thai food. I enjoyed the noodle soup (Laksa-more Malay than Thai) and the chicken Kharpow especially. The flavors were authentic and satisfying. Desert servings of ice cream, coconut milk and sticky toffee were exceptional, and most us went for seconds. This venue is very well managed, and the host was constantly around ensuring everything was running smooth. The bar was well stocked and even a simple fresh lime soda was made to perfevtion. Overall, this is a must do place.

text.text:
Found hair in our food, extremely unhygienic
We ordered paneer paratha from Kapoor Cafe and were shocked to find multiple small hairs mixed into the food. This is a serious food safety and hygiene violation. It's not a one-off crumb or minor issue — there were several strands, which points to a real lapse in kitchen cleanliness, staff hygiene practices (like not wearing hairnets/caps), or food handling standards.
For a place serving food to the public, this is unacceptable. We couldn't finish the meal and had to throw it away. I'd strongly advise the management to review their kitchen hygiene protocols — staff should be wearing proper caps/hairnets while cooking and packing food, and there should be a final quality check before food leaves the kitchen.
Very disappointed, and I won't be ordering from here again. Would not recommend to anyone who cares about food safety.

text.text:
Visited Kapoor's Cafe on a Sunday night around 9:30 PM, mainly because we had heard they serve good North Indian food.

Location & Setup:

The cafe is located on the 4th floor (with the kitchen on the 3rd). The seating area has a proper North Indian vibe—regular table-chair setups along with khat-style seating, which adds a nice rustic touch.

Crowd & Service:

The place was completely packed, easily accommodating around 70–90 people. We had to wait about 10 minutes, which is reasonable for a weekend. However, a major issue was understaffing—only around 3 servers managing the entire crowd, plus one person cleaning tables. This led to slow and inefficient service, which was noticeable throughout.

What we ordered:

Paneer Pakoda (₹340, 8 pieces)
Aloo Paratha (₹180)
Punjabi Chole Thali (₹340)
Lemonade / Lemon Soda
Chaach

Food Review:

Paneer Pakoda (2.5/5):
Quantity felt less for the price. The paneer didn’t taste fresh, which was disappointing. The chutney served alongside was good, but it couldn’t compensate for the average pakodas.

Aloo Paratha (1/5):

Looked promising initially—good size and decent stuffing quantity. But the taste was extremely bland. It felt like plain mashed potatoes stuffed inside, with no seasoning or flavor. Easily the most disappointing dish of the night.

Punjabi Chole Thali (2.5/5):

Chole: The only highlight—really well made.
Chapati: Good size, but didn’t feel fresh.
Rice: Too much ghee (subjective, but didn’t work for me).
Dal & Raita: Average.
Missing Salad: A basic salad wasn’t included, which is usually standard with thalis—felt like a miss, especially at this price point.

Lemon Soda (1/5):
Completely flat—no fizz at all. Didn’t feel like a proper soda.
Chaach (3/5):
Decent and as expected, nothing special.

Overall Verdict:

The ambience and seating concept are good, and the place has potential. But the food quality is disappointing across most items, especially considering the pricing. Service also suffers due to lack of staff.

Honestly, not a place I’d revisit or recommend. There are far better North Indian options in HSR Layout that offer better taste and value for money.

I’ve been eating at SLV coffee bar since the late 1990s and it’s still my go-to for quick, no-nonsense South Indian food.

*Idly + Chutney* is excellent - soft, fluffy idlys and that chutney hits the right spot every time. Fair warning though: they don’t serve sambar, only chutney, so if you’re a sambar person, plan accordingly.

*Coffee* is proper darshini-style - strong, frothy, and exactly what you want with your breakfast. *Service is super quick*, true to the darshini setup. You order, you get it, you’re out - perfect for mornings when you’re in a rush.

*Medu Vada* is very good - crisp outside, soft inside. *Khara Bath* and the other South Indian snacks are always served fresh and taste delicious.

Been coming here for 25+ years and the consistency hasn’t dropped. If you want authentic, fast, fuss-free South Indian breakfast, SLV still delivers.

text.text:
Shri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Coffee Bar is not merely a place to eat; it is a living chapter of Bengaluru’s culinary heritage. One of the city’s oldest and most cherished establishments, this coffee bar has stood the test of time by doing one simple thing exceptionally well—serving honest, soulful South Indian food with unwavering consistency.

The idlis here deserve special mention. Soft, cloud-like, and perfectly steamed, they soak up flavours beautifully and set the tone for a truly satisfying meal. Paired with their legendary chutneys, every bite feels comforting and nostalgic. The masala dosa is another clear winner—golden, crisp on the outside, yet delicately soft within, generously filled and cooked to perfection. Their Golden Roast crispy dosa, in particular, is a showstopper: thin, evenly roasted, audibly crisp, and bursting with flavour, it reflects years of mastery over the art of dosa-making.

What truly elevates this place, however, is the chutney. The gatti chutney is rich, bold, and textured, while the neer chutney is light, fluid, and refreshingly balanced. Together, they create a harmonious contrast that complements every dish on the plate. The vade is crunchy on the outside, soft and airy inside, with just the right seasoning—exactly how a classic vada should be.

Beyond the staples, the menu offers comforting favourites like avalakki, flavourful palao, aromatic khara bath, and perfectly balanced kesari bath, each prepared with care and traditional finesse. To conclude the meal, their filter coffee is outstanding—strong, aromatic, and served piping hot, leaving a lingering, satisfying finish.

Shri Lakshmi Venkateshwara Coffee Bar is a timeless institution that continues to win hearts across generations. If you wish to experience authentic Bengaluru breakfast culture in its purest form, this place is an absolute must-visit.

text.text:
I had a wonderful experience at Stories Bar & Kitchen, Rajajinagar. We ordered boiled peanuts, masala cashew crispy, kadai paneer, garlic butter naan, and lacha paratha. The boiled peanuts were a simple yet comforting start, while the masala cashew crispy really stood out – well coated with spices, perfectly crunchy, and addictive with every bite.

The kadai paneer was outstanding – the paneer was soft and fresh, cooked with cubes of onion and capsicum in a flavorful masala that had just the right balance of spice and richness. It paired beautifully with the breads. The garlic butter naan was aromatic, soft, and loaded with butter, while the lacha paratha was layered and flaky, adding a nice variety to the meal.

Overall, everything we tried was excellent, and the dining experience was truly enjoyable. A special mention to Diwakar and Sushant for their attentive and warm service – they really made the evening memorable with their professionalism and hospitality.

text.text:
This 55 year old restaurant, undoubtedly, unquestionably, serves the best Khali dose in all of Bengaluru. At times even doctors recommend patients to have dose here. The texture is so Spongy and fluffy with a million pores in it. It's served with 2 dallops of butter & palya upon request & at an extra cost of ₹20, otherwise with just neer chutney. It's simply the best form of dose that you can get. The most surprising part of this is that, the doses are cooked & roasted without a single drop of oil or ghee or butter. It's simply amazing how a humble dose can be so overwhelming in taste.
I was recommended the vade in sambar dip, which was good but not excellent in taste, it's evident that they do not use adulterants to cook these items. Apart from that you get amazing pineapple Kesari bath, avarekaalu uppittu, poori sagu here. Sundays are famous for their carrot halwa. Also, Sundays are famous for the tomato dose that they prepare which apparently isn't available anywhere else across the city.
The perfect ending to this meal is a handsome glass of Filter Coffee. The flavor & temperature is so well achieved with perfection, it just tastes heavenly. This place is always crowded for the taste they provide, it's Bengaluru's pride & legacy on a plate surely!
