I always expect better from reputed places. Unfortunately, my recent Zomato order from here (over ₹1,500) turned out to be one of the most disappointing experiences I've had in a long time.

I ordered Gobi Manchurian, Hyderabadi Veg Biryani, Chicken 65 (boneless), and Hyderabadi Boneless Chicken Biryani. What arrived was unacceptable on every level:

1. Chicken 65 (boneless): Nearly inedible. Almost 90% of the pieces were just skin and fat, hardly any real meat. The little meat that was there was rubbery, dry, and badly overcooked. This feels dishonest and completely unfair for the price paid.

2. Hyderabadi Boneless Chicken Biryani & Hyderabadi Veg Biryani: Both were shockingly poor. The rice was completely bland, tasteless, and had zero seasoning or aroma. There was no flavor whatsoever...it barely qualified as biryani. The texture was mushy and lifeless. Extremely disappointing.

3. Gobi Manchurian: This was the only item that was even remotely acceptable. Everything else was a total failure.

I have attached the bill for reference (total ₹1,521.98). For this amount, the quality fell far, far...FAR below any reasonable standard. I am deeply disappointed and frustrated with such substandard food from a place that carries a famous name.

I demand a full refund of the entire amount immediately. Please treat this seriously and confirm the refund without delay. If a full refund isn't possible, provide a clear explanation and a satisfactory compensatory solution right away.

I stay 5-6km away from the restaurant and the order was delivered within 50 min from the time of order, so distance cannot be a factor for food quality here.

This experience has left me utterly let down. I will not be ordering from here again.

text.text:
⭐⭐⭐☆☆

Visited La Casa recently and had a decent overall experience. The beer was definitely the highlight of the visit. The brews were fresh, well-crafted, and enjoyable. If you're someone who likes trying different beers, this place is worth considering.

That said, I felt the food could be improved. It wasn't bad by any means, but it didn't stand out either. When I compare it with places like Bier Library or Roxie, I would say those breweries currently have a stronger food menu and a more memorable dining experience. At La Casa, the food felt average and lacked the wow factor that I usually look for when spending on a brewery outing.

The ambiance is pleasant and comfortable, but the place itself is relatively small compared to many of the newer breweries that have opened in Bangalore over the last few years. Newer venues offer larger spaces, better seating options, and a more vibrant atmosphere for groups and weekend outings.

The pricing is another factor. Since La Casa is priced similarly to Bier Library, Roxie, and some of the other premium breweries in the area, it naturally invites comparison. At the same price point, I personally find myself preferring Bier Library or Roxie because of their stronger food offerings and overall experience.

Having said that, La Casa has one major advantage for me—it's close to home. For a casual evening beer, a quick meetup with friends, or when I don't want to travel far through Bangalore traffic, it's still a convenient option. Overall, it's a decent neighborhood brewery with good beer, but I feel there is room for improvement in the food and overall value proposition.

text.text:
Nandana Palace is a well-known name for Andhra-style cuisine, and my recent visit was a fairly decent experience overall. The food remains the main highlight of this place. The menu offers a good variety of spicy and flavourful Andhra dishes, especially for those who enjoy bold masalas and traditional preparations. The biryani was aromatic and well-cooked, with tender pieces of meat and balanced spices. Starters were served hot and tasted fresh, making them enjoyable. Portion sizes are reasonable for the price, and the food quality is consistent, which is reassuring for repeat visits.

However, the ambiance is where Nandana Palace falls a bit short. While the restaurant is clean and functional, it lacks warmth and aesthetic appeal. The seating arrangement feels slightly cramped during peak hours, and the interiors are quite basic, offering nothing memorable or inviting. It feels more like a quick dining spot rather than a place to relax and enjoy a leisurely meal with family or friends. Noise levels can also rise when the restaurant gets busy, which affects the overall dining comfort.

Service was satisfactory, with staff being responsive and fairly quick to take orders and serve food, though nothing exceptional. Overall, Nandana Palace is a good option if you’re specifically craving authentic Andhra food and prioritise taste over ambiance. With some improvement in interiors and atmosphere, the dining experience could be significantly better. For now, it’s best suited for food-focused visits rather than special occasions or long, relaxed outings.

text.text:
One of the oldest roof top pubs in Bengaluru. I've been going there since 2011 and it never gets old. The food is excellent, I loved the California rolls, grilled prawn and their burgers.

The view during sun set is spectacular and it's worth getting a seat near the edge, although, it gets freezing cold, it's highly recommended that you pack yourself to keep warm.

There is a cover charge on entry which is redeemable/minused on the total bill. For a couple on a Friday night we were charged Rs 2,500. The staff get very busy during peak hours and it could be pretty tough to get hold of them.

If you just go for the food, ambience and the experience it will be pretty light on your pocket. Purchasing of any alcoholic beverages will get increase your bill significantly.

The indoor lounge is calm and soft feels just like a regular place. Prior booking of table is a MUST! as tables are very difficult to get during the weekends. Paying through zomato or swiggy may reduce your total bill due to discounts sometimes, so its worth checking.

I recently visited Skyye and overall, it was a good experience, but not without its flaws.

The place definitely stands out for its aesthetics - the rooftop vibe, lighting, and overall ambience are beautiful. It felt quite peaceful, probably because we visited on a weekday, so it wasn’t too crowded. If you're going purely for the vibe and pictures, it does deliver.

Coming to the food, it was decent but not perfect. We had to switch our order twice, which was a bit frustrating. Eventually, we tried the chicken pasta, feta cheese dish, fruit melon bowl, and a salad. The taste was good, nothing exceptional, but satisfactory.

Where the place really fell short was the service. It wasn’t up to the mark for a place of this level. The delays and order issues made it feel a bit overhyped.

Honestly, Skyye feels more like a place you should visit during weekends or late evenings when the party vibe is on. That’s probably when the ambience truly shines. On a regular weekday, it feels a bit underwhelming.

Overall: good aesthetics, decent food, average service – more hype than substance unless you time your visit right.

text.text:
We recently visited Barbeque Nation on a Sunday. For 6 people (3 veg & 3 non-veg), the total bill came to around ₹4,500.

First thing—this place is definitely more suitable for non-veg lovers. Veg options felt quite limited for the price. Veg starters included paneer, mushroom, and sweet corn (crispy corn was actually very tasty), but most items were just variations of the same ingredients.

On the non-veg side, they served chicken, fish, prawns, and mutton.

Chicken was good 👍

Fish was average

Prawns were okay

Mutton pieces were very small and honestly tasted more like soya/milmaker than real mutton

Coming to the buffet (self-service):

Chicken biryani had almost no chicken

Chicken curry & fish curry were available

Egg fried rice was decent

Very limited egg-based dishes (they should add more)

Mutton kurma was there but nothing special

Veg gravies and fry items were quite limited

Desserts were basic:

Only vanilla & strawberry ice cream

2 types of cakes

Gulab jamun (good) + one more sweet

Pani puri was unlimited

Fruits, sprouts, curd rice, and salads were available

Major concern:
We found a ⚠️cockroach stuck to the kulfi stick, which was very disappointing and concerning. Hygiene needs serious attention. I strongly suggest checking food items properly before eating.

Service was fast and staff were polite. Soft drinks are charged separately. They offer a free cake for birthdays or special occasions.

Final Verdict:
Average experience overall. Not worth the price for veg customers, and hygiene issues make it worse. If you still want to visit, book early for discounts and be cautious with food.

Some restaurants simply serve food, while others create an experience—and Oyster Bar & Restaurant definitely belongs to the latter.

From the moment we walked in, the vibrant ambiance and warm hospitality made us feel comfortable. Being pet-friendly was a lovely surprise, making it a great spot for families and pet lovers alike.

The menu is a dream for food enthusiasts, offering everything from delicious duck preparations to an impressive selection of fresh seafood. Every dish we ordered had its own unique character. The Ghee Roast Duck was the highlight of the evening—succulent, flavorful, and perfectly coated with aromatic spices. The Butter Garlic Prawns were fresh, tender, and bursting with rich buttery goodness. The Crab Toast was crispy on the outside with a deliciously flavorful filling, while the Crispy Corn was light, crunchy, and impossible to stop munching on.

What made the experience even better was the attentive and friendly staff, who ensured everything was served perfectly and made us feel genuinely welcome.

If you're looking for a place that combines amazing food, fresh seafood, unique duck dishes, a relaxed atmosphere, and the bonus of being pet-friendly, Oyster Bar & Restaurant is a place you'll want to visit again and again. Every bite was memorable, and we left with happy hearts, full stomachs, and wonderful memories...

text.text:
Purani Dilli offers a satisfying overall experience with flavors that largely live up to expectations, though there are a couple of areas that could use some attention. The food, in general, is enjoyable and well-prepared, capturing the essence of North Indian street-style cuisine. The masala puri, while tasty, leans slightly on the heavier side in terms of spice and seasoning. For those who prefer a more balanced or lighter masala, it might feel a bit overwhelming after a few bites. That said, the quality of ingredients and freshness are evident, and the rest of the menu items we tried were well-executed and flavorful.

The ambiance and service inside the establishment were pleasant, contributing to a comfortable dining experience. However, the biggest drawback during our visit was related to parking management. The watchman seemed unaware of the actual parking availability, which led to confusion and miscommunication. Unfortunately, this resulted in an unpleasant interaction with another customer who believed we had taken up a spot incorrectly. This situation could have easily been avoided with better coordination and clarity regarding parking space allocation.

While such incidents may not reflect the overall quality of the restaurant itself, they do impact the customer experience significantly. A little more organization and communication from the staff handling parking would go a long way in ensuring a smoother visit for guests.

Overall, Purani Dilli delivers on taste and variety, making it a place worth visiting for its food. With some improvements in external management, especially parking coordination, the experience could become much more seamless and enjoyable.

📍 Anand Sweets | Whitefield, Bangalore

For anyone craving authentic North Indian flavours in Bangalore, Anand Sweets in Whitefield continues to be a dependable and much-loved destination. It’s a place that delivers consistency, comfort, and familiarity—visit after visit.

🌶️ Food & Taste

We tried a good mix of their offerings, and everything lived up to expectations.
•	The winter special – makke ki roti and sarson ka saag was the clear highlight: rustic, flavourful, and wonderfully authentic, just the way it should be.
•	Their regular thali is equally impressive—well-balanced, satisfying, and a great representation of classic North Indian home-style food.
•	The chaat items were fresh and well assembled, and the jalebi was crisp on the outside, soft inside, and perfectly syrupy.

Across categories—meals, chaat, and sweets—the taste was consistent, comforting, and reliable.

🧼 Hygiene & Cleanliness

As expected from Anand Sweets, hygiene standards are top-notch. The outlet is clean, well organised, and inspires confidence, especially for dine-in and chaat items.

💰 Pricing & Value for Money

Prices are fair and justified for the quality, portion sizes, and overall experience. You get solid value for money, especially given the consistency in taste.

🧑‍🍳 Service & Speed

Service is efficient and professional, handling orders smoothly even during busy hours.

🌟 Overall Experience

If you’re in Bangalore, this place is a must-visit.

text.text:
Cool Corner in V.V. Puram has been my go-to spot since childhood, and it continues to be one of the best places for South Indian food, especially their Masala Dosa, which, in my opinion, is the finest I’ve had. Served with two chutneys and a flavorful sagu, the dosa is consistently crispy and perfectly spiced, though the chutneys tend to range between spicy and extremely spicy. Apart from their exceptional dosas, they also offer a good variety of sandwiches and shakes, making it a great spot for both traditional and quick bites.

One of the standout aspects of this place is its very quick service, ensuring that you get your food fresh and hot in no time. However, during peak hours, especially in the evenings or weekends, you might have to wait for about 5-10 minutes due to the high demand. The ambiance is simple yet nostalgic, adding to its charm, and the pricing is quite reasonable for the quality they offer.

While almost everything here impresses, the only slight letdown is their coffee, which is quite average compared to the rest of their offerings. That being said, if you're in the area and craving a delicious Masala Dosa or a refreshing shake, Cool Corner is definitely worth a visit!

text.text:
Most happening place to visit and the food here won't cost a fortune.
It's a super popular spot, and as soon as you walk in, you can feel the good vibes. The place looks cool and inviting, perfect for hanging out with friends.

The food is really tasty, and the prices are easy on your wallet. They have lots of different dishes, so you're sure to find something you like. The portions are suitable for small group too, so you definitely get your money's worth.

The people who work there are super friendly, which makes the whole experience even better. Basically, Chin Lung is a great place to go if you want a fun time, good food, and don't want to spend too much money. I totally recommend it!

We had a wonderful time here for lunch. The menu is packed with amazing, delectable dishes. We kicked things off with the Korean garlic bun, which was an absolute standout. The Sherpa’s jhol momos and truffle edamame dumplings followed, both hitting the mark perfectly. We also loved the Banarasi litti chokha, which was scrumptious and authentically prepared. The veg biryani main course was decent, but the desserts were the real grand finale—both the pull-me-up tiramisu and the Vietnamese coffee tres leches were pure heaven.

To top it all off, the service was polite and cheerful. A special mention to Jeni, whose service was incredibly hospitable and great!

In fact, a waiter called Rongzalu also tried to sneak in a family without their name itself in the list inspite of us waiting with a kid in the scorching sun for more than 40 minutes. Once you’re inside, the service is just decent.

Food - 4/5 based on taste.

Overall, no owner or manager were present and this place seems to be running only by waiters and the security guard. No maintenance at all. Avoid if you respect your time and love your body.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a relaxed dining spot in central Bangalore,  on Cunningham/Infantry Road Eden Park Restaurant is worth a visit. The restaurant has a calm, old-Bangalore charm with plenty of greenery and comfortable seating that works well for family dinners, casual outings, and small get-togethers.

The menu offers a good mix of Andhra, North Indian, Chinese, and seafood dishes,

We tried the Andhra Biryani, meals, Mutton Fry, and Chicken Kabab. The Andhra Biryani was fairly average and didn’t particularly stand out, but the meals were simple, comforting, and quite enjoyable in a homely way.
What truly sets the place apart is the ambience. The restaurant is surrounded by lush greenery, and the sounds of birds — even if played over speakers — create a calm, relaxing atmosphere that feels like a little oasis in the middle of Bangalore’s bustle. A good spot if you’re looking more for a peaceful dining experience than an extravagant meal.

text.text:
The iconic New Modern Hotel (NMH) in VV Puram, Bangalore, is legendary for its authentic, traditional South Indian breakfast and snacks.
​Here is what makes their star dishes stand out:
​Khali Dose: Super soft, fluffy, and perfectly porous, served with a generous dollop of butter and their signature chutney.
​Masale Dose: Notably different from the typical Bengaluru Vidyarthi Bhavan style; it has a distinct, golden-brown crispness without being overly greasy, paired with a flavorful potato palya.
​Bread Dish (Bread Toast/Cutlet): A nostalgic, old-school favorite. Their bread toast features perfectly crisped bread slathered with butter and a unique spice mix, while the bread masala/cutlet options offer a perfect savory crunch.
​Idli Vade Sambar: The idlis are cloud-soft, the vada is incredibly crunchy on the outside, and it is all served with a traditional, slightly sweet, and highly aromatic Karnataka-style sambar.
Finally Filter coffee with moderate sugar is super.

Was here 2 days ago only for Breakfast. It has a slightly yesteryear charm, not fancy like the current 'Cafes' of Bangalore... But the Food was yum, reminding one of yester years. Started with Coffee... much better than many places.. Then Idly and Vada.. the vada was real fresh and crisp and with true taste of Uddina Bele (Urad Dal), which is "rare" in todays eateries. The sambar was 5 star , hot, and one Bucket Sambar, Kept on each table, that was unique .
Masala dose was yum, crispy and generous helping of masala. Khara bath , was good , but should be called just plain uppitu. It was not khara bath. Poori and sagu was normal, nothing great, but good old style, pure atta poori (no traces of maida).  One last unique item was the "Toast" (homestyle, tava toasted with ghee) served with a unique combination of sagu n their own liquid jam. I liked it ...
Good place to get a yester year charm.

text.text:
Bad experience. Never going to buy any product from them. They sell old, rotten products with dubious expiry dates.

As the name says, you expect fresh bakery products to be sold by Iyengars. But it's not so.

I bought a box of Focaccia bread from them thinking that it'll be fresh. But the very next day I saw fungus growing on it. Which should not have happened, if the product was freshly made.

Due to this, I took the box back to the shop and requested for a refund.

To my surprise, the shop owners were so stubborn that instead of giving me a refund they started arguing and stating that we don't give refunds, you take another packet of the bread in place of this one.

Why? Because they have a policy that they don't refund money. Even when they sell rotten products.

Not just this, they also gave me reasons like if you buy a refrigerator, if there's a problem, it is replaced and no refund is given. Same way we are willing to replace not refund.

In which world, a bread (consumable product) can be compared to a refrigerator (kitchen appliance). This argument made me understand that the owners don't know what they are selling and what is the product category.

And if they don't know how food business works then obviously how will they cater to their customers.

Such bad customer service is a given, with brands like Iyengars.

And therefore I don't trust the food quality at all. More so when you say oven fresh but sell bakery items that are not fresh.

text.text:
Not every restaurant makes you go "Wow!" the moment you walk in. Some earn that feeling through their food, while some do it through their ambience. Maize & Malt is one of those rare places that manages to do both.

🍽 Food – ⭐⭐⭐⭐⭐ (5/5)
This was honestly the highlight of the evening. Everything we ordered was served hot, tasted great, and reached our table without an unnecessarily long wait.
The Kerala Pork (recommended by the staff) and the Crispy Chicken were definitely my favourites. The Guava Chilli Mocktail was refreshing and paired really well with the food.
But the real showstoppers were the desserts. Mango Panna Cotta and Mango Pull Me Up completely blew my mind. The presentation, texture, and taste... everything was just spot on.
Another thing I really appreciated was their willingness to customize a dish to our preferred spice level. It's these small things that definitely earn them brownie points.

🏛️ Ambience –  (4/5)
The first thing that catches your attention is how massive this place is. Even on a packed Sunday evening, it never felt crowded or chaotic. The seating is spacious, comfortable, and there's enough breathing space to actually enjoy your time.
The warm lighting, beautiful architecture, greenery, and the balcony overlooking the ground floor all add to the experience. I can only imagine how beautiful this place would look around sunset.
The live music was enjoyable, although sitting close to the stage on the first floor can make conversations a little difficult. Everywhere else, the music volume was just right.
Clean washrooms and valet parking are definitely added brownie points.

🤝 Service – (4/5)
The staff was courteous, attentive, and knew the menu really well. In fact, the Kerala Pork recommendation came from them, and it turned out to be one of the best dishes we ordered.
Despite the restaurant being packed, there was always someone nearby whenever we needed assistance. We never had to wait long to place another order or ask for anything, which was quite impressive.

✅ Overall
If you're looking for a place that offers great food, beautiful ambience, and equally good service, Maize & Malt is definitely worth visiting. It's one of those places I'd happily visit again—not just for the food, but for the complete dining experience.

Parking seemed to be mostly along the roadside, though we didn't face any major issues during our visit.

Overall, we enjoyed our time here. If you're looking for a place with a great ambience for team lunches or group gatherings around Whitefield and Mahadevapura, this is a good option.

text.text:
South Thindis is a perfect example of Bengaluru’s beloved darshini-style breakfast culture—quick, comforting, and full of character. Located near Krishna Rao Park, the spot is instantly recognizable thanks to its eye-catching metallic installation at the entrance.

Revisiting this place brings a wave of nostalgia, especially for those who’ve been coming here since its early days. It’s the kind of place where you can stop by for a quick bite or linger a little longer with a cup of filter coffee, enjoying the relaxed, old-Bangalore vibe. The veranda-style setup adds to that charm, making it a great place to unwind or casually catch up with friends.

One of the highlights is the smooth and modern ordering system. The self-service kiosks make placing orders quick and hassle-free, even during busy hours. Despite the crowd, the service remains efficient, and the place is consistently clean and hygienic.

The menu is extensive, covering all the classic “thindi” favorites. Items like idli, vada, and khara bath are well-prepared and satisfying, even if you might find softer idlis elsewhere. The rava dosa stands out as a must-try—crispy, flavorful, and absolutely worth it. There are also plenty of interesting options like ragi rotti, akki rotti, neer dosa (available after noon), sabbasige dosa, Mangalore buns, and even Kerala parota, offering something for every craving.

In the evenings, the place comes alive with snacks like bonda and bajji, making it a great all-day destination. With reasonable pricing, quick turnaround, and a wide variety of dishes, it’s an ideal spot for a hearty breakfast or a casual snack break. Definitely worth checking out if you’re in the area.

text.text:
Xero Degrees is a good spot if you’re in the mood for desserts, mocktais, and pizza, all under one roof. The place has a lively vibe, especially in the evenings, and works well for catching up with friends or just grabbing a quick bite.

The menu is quite varied, with options like loaded fries, burgers, pizzas, and their popular jar desserts. The food tastes good overall and definitely satisfying. The loaded fries stand out with generous toppings, and the burgers are filling enough for one person. Their desserts, especially the thick shakes and jar cakes, are worth trying if you have a sweet tooth.

Portion sizes are decent, so you feel like you’re getting your money’s worth. Pricing is reasonable.

The ambience is quirky and modern, with bright lighting and comfortable seating. It does its job well as a hangout spot. Service is fairly quick, even during busy hours, and the staff is polite.

Overall, Xero Degrees is a reliable option when you want something indulgent and easygoing. It is consistent, enjoyable, and a place you can revisit without overthinking.

text.text:
We visited The Local on a Friday evening around 7 PM as a group of five. The place was not very crowded initially, and although we hadn’t pre-booked a table, we were comfortably seated. By around 9 PM, the crowd gradually increased, which added to the lively atmosphere.

We ordered a variety of dishes and beverages during our visit. The Chicken Sausages with Veggies did not match our expectations, as the overall flavours didn’t come together well for us. The Peri Peri French Fries were enjoyable, and we liked them enough to order Plain Salty Fries, which were also good. The Fully Loaded Cheese Nachos (Veg) were decent.

The Barbecue Chicken Wings were not to our taste, and we felt they might not have been prepared to the level we expected. We also tried the Mexican Veg Pizza and the Smoked Chicken Pizza; while I personally found the chicken pizza acceptable, the group as a whole did not prefer the pizzas, and we were unable to finish them.

For drinks, most of us opted for bottled beer (Budweiser pint). Larger bottles were not available, and tap beer was the primary option. Some of us tried the Hefeweizen Pint and Banger Lager Pint, which felt a bit diluted. A couple of cocktails, including a flavoured mojito and a shot (possibly Brain Damage), didn’t quite suit our preferences. On the positive side, the whisky trio combo, featuring Red Label and Jack Daniel’s, was well received by the group.

We initially considered ordering more cocktails, including a LIIT, but after trying one and finding it not quite aligned with our taste, we decided not to continue further. Again, this is purely based on our individual preferences.

The ambience was pleasant, and we noticed posters about open-mic comedy events, which seemed interesting. Parking was convenient, and two-wheeler parking was available right outside.

While our overall experience with the food and drinks did not fully meet our expectations, we understand that taste is subjective, and what may not work for us could be appreciated by others. Our intention is not to criticize but to share honest feedback so the team can take it constructively. On a lighter note, we noticed a small typo (“Frise” instead of “Fries”) on the bill, just sharing with a smile 😊.

Wishing the team at The Local all the best, and we appreciate the service and hospitality extended to us during our visit. Cheers!

Anand Sweets in Koramangala is hands down one of the finest places for authentic Indian sweets and snacks! Every visit here feels special — from the warm hospitality to the elegant presentation, everything reflects quality and tradition. I’ve been a regular customer for years, and their consistency and attention to detail never fail to impress.

My absolute favorites are their Matka Rabdi, Kaaju Katli, and Motichoor Laddu — each one is pure perfection! The Matka Rabdi is rich, creamy, and has that perfect balance of sweetness and flavor, served beautifully in a traditional matka that enhances the experience. The Kaaju Katli melts in your mouth with its fine texture and pure cashew taste, while the Motichoor Laddu is soft, fragrant, and tastes just like something made with love at home.

I also absolutely love their Badamika Biscotti — it’s crunchy, nutty, and makes for the perfect snack with tea or coffee. It’s something I always make sure to pick up whenever I visit. Anand Sweets is also my go-to place for gifting, because their packaging is elegant and festive, and the quality is always top-notch — guests absolutely love receiving sweets from here!

The staff are polite, helpful, and always make you feel welcome. The store itself is clean, well-organized, and has a lovely aroma that instantly tempts you to try everything.

Overall, Anand Sweets in Koramangala is a true symbol of premium quality, taste, and Indian tradition. A well-deserved five-star experience every single time!

text.text:
Planning for a romantic date? or a family get-together?
Here's the perfect place for you.

This olive beach, the Mediterranean restaurant located in Ashok Nagar looks stunning with its beautiful interiors, the colorful drapes and art pieces against the white theme gives exotic vibes and the natural plants just enhance the beauty of the place.

It offers both indoors and outdoor seating arrangements, both of these come with their own benefits, the indoor looks more like a sophisticated cafe with easy chairs and controlled temperature, whereas the outdoor seating arrangement comes with beautiful drapes hanging from the ceilings, uncomfortably beautiful sofas with exceptionally small tables for 3 people and a live karaoke with lots of sweat because of the amazing whether of the bengaluru during peak summertime(Thanks to summer 2026).

We were almost the first to arrive on a sunday afternoon(12:00), my friend had booked a table for 3, they directed us to a table which is located at the outdoors despite we requested for an indoor table(Yes, we wanted to have a cool and breezy air of an AC), But the staff politely declined our request saying that, the indoor tables are only for 4 and more, since we were 3, we had to sit outside. Surprisingly the table which we sat later was also a 4 seater. The staff needs to be trained more on how to give better excuses.

While we sat on our table, We saw an inhouse photographer who was clicking photographs of random customers except us, In my defence we were well dressed and we were looking pretty.
It's okay,by looking at the way he was clicking the pictures, he didn't appear to be good at his own skills.

The best thing about the our afternoon was this beautiful girl Ms,Ranjani singing on a live katoke, Amazing voice, very graceful and very pretty, I wanted to send her a request to sing one of my favorite songs(They said they were open for requests), I asked multiple times to the waiters(I usually try to avid this word and I refer to them as staff, but the way they behaved I had to use it) but they ignored it.
Luckily I met this girl near the washroom(Btw the washroom looked great, I loved the interiors) and I requested her to sing "Rolling in the Deep". She acknowledged and sang it exceptionally well.

Oh I forgot about the food, who cares...!
Maybe next time, Let them work on their hospitality and skill development training for their staff.

The rating is 2.5 but grounding it to 2

text.text:
⭐ Rating: ★★☆☆☆ (2/5)

I recently visited Masala Mandi, Sarjapur after watching a few videos online that made the place look really promising — vibrant ambience, great food variety, and a lively dining experience. While the ambience and service were indeed good, the overall food experience didn’t quite live up to the expectations set by the videos.

Starting with the positives — the restaurant has a pleasant and well-decorated setting that creates a nice dining atmosphere. The staff members were polite, attentive, and genuinely tried to make sure guests were comfortable, which I really appreciated. Service was quick and the team was courteous throughout.

However, when it comes to the food, I felt there’s significant room for improvement. Many of the dishes looked appealing but lacked authentic flavour. The taste didn’t quite match what was showcased online — it seemed that several items were made with a lot of soda or artificial ingredients, which left a heavy aftertaste and took away from the freshness one expects in Indian cuisine.

Another disappointing aspect was the drinks menu. Although the restaurant lists a good range of beverages, most of them were unavailable. It felt odd to be charged for drinks that weren’t even in stock or to have very limited options in what was supposed to be a full-fledged dining experience.

Overall, Masala Mandi has potential — the ambience and service are definitely its strengths. But if the restaurant wants to live up to its online reputation, it really needs to focus on improving the taste and authenticity of its dishes and maintaining consistency in what’s offered on the menu.

text.text:
Raghavendra Stores is one of those cult-favorite Bangalore breakfast spots that keeps things simple and traditional. It’s not about ambience or comfort here it’s all about quick, authentic South Indian food at very affordable prices.

The food is straightforward but satisfying

* The idli is genuinely great for the price, soft, comforting, and easy to keep going back for.
* The shavige bath was also good, light and flavorful.
* The chutney had a nice pudina hint, which added a fresh touch without overpowering the dish.

That said, the place is almost always crowded, and there’s barely any seating available. Most people end up standing and eating, which is part of the experience at this point.

The biggest advantage is definitely the pricing, which is extremely reasonable and makes the place feel very worth it.

Ambrosia is an amazing place — truly one of the first vegetarian restaurants I’ve been fully impressed with. The space is clean, well-designed, and has the vibe of a sports bar with huge screens. It’s spacious, serves liquor, and the prices are very reasonable. We ordered a variety of dishes and everything tasted great — flavourful food without the “filler” soda effect that many restaurants rely on.

Even after eating a lot, our bill came to only ₹3.5K for five people, which is excellent compared to similar large restaurants. The option of both open and indoor seating is a big plus as well.

The only drawback was that several items listed online — like thalis and chaat — weren’t available when we visited. Since many customers choose restaurants based on menu items they see online, this can be a bit disappointing.

That said, I still highly recommend Ambrosia for its great food, service, ambience, and overall value. A must-visit for vegetarians.

text.text:
Tried the Death By Chocolate. Came to ₹263 including GST and comfortably served two people. Rich chocolate-heavy dessert with layers of cake, vanilla ice cream, hot fudge, peanuts, cream, and cherries. The texture balance is good and the portion size justifies the price.

The outlet itself is compact, with seating for roughly 17 people across 5 tables, so it can feel crowded during peak hours. Ambience is functional rather than premium, but service was quick and the dessert quality holds up to the brand’s reputation.

Overall: 4/5. Good value, generous portions, and still one of the better quick dessert stops for classic chocolate sundaes.

For the amount being charged, this level of food quality and service is simply unacceptable. Definitely not the experience we expected from such a well-known place.

Definitely a spot I keep coming back to for good food, good beer, and a relaxed vibe. 🍕🍺✨

Siddiq Kabab Centre near Johnson Market is truly an OG place when it comes to seekh kababs and Beef kalmi kaba. If you are a beef lover, this spot is an absolute must-visit in Bangalore.

text.text:
Extremely disappointing experience. I visited this restaurant expecting good food and decent service, but it turned out to be one of the worst dining experiences I've had.I ordered the North Indian meal based on the cashier's recommendation. Unfortunately, it was nowhere near worth the high price I paid. The meal was incomplete—they forgot to serve the salad and papad, and I had to remind them before they brought them. This basic lack of attention to customers is unacceptable.
The food quality was very poor. The curries were bland, lacked proper seasoning, and tasted stale rather than freshly prepared. The overall meal had no authentic North Indian flavor and was far below expectations. For the price they charge, customers deserve fresh, flavorful food, not something that feels like it has been sitting for hours.The restaurant's hygiene standards also need serious improvement. Although the place is relatively new, it already appears poorly maintained. The dining area was not clean enough, and the overall atmosphere did not inspire confidence. There was no proper RO drinking water facility; instead, they were serving water from a bubble-top can. This made me question whether they even use purified water for cooking.The seating arrangement was also uncomfortable and not well maintained, making the dining experience even less enjoyable.Overall, this restaurant is charging premium prices without delivering the quality, hygiene, or service that customers expect. I regret choosing this place based on the recommendation given at the counter. I hope the management takes customer feedback seriously and improves the food quality, cleanliness, and service. Until then, I cannot recommend this restaurant to anyone.

text.text:
I've been going to the MG Road metro station for about ten years, but until today, I never had the opportunity to go to this cafe, which is directly in front of the station.

The cafe has got very cool vibes and hosts both indoor and outdoor seating arrangements. We decided to have a table inside for obvious reasons.
The steats were very comfortable and tables were spaced properly with a good amount of space between two tables so that we wouldn't hear the conversation form the next table.

We ordered an espresso shot, a cold coffee(for me) and some water based tea for my friend. The cold coffee was really amazing with a perfect blend of coffee and cold milk. My friends said their drinks were good but mine was the best (they did taste the cold coffee from my cup).

The interesting part about the washroom, it's made of steel and looks like a giant refrigerator, its really high time they should change the mirror and interiors of the men's washroom(cutting down a star for this).

Had a great time here. Great place if you are planning to hangout with your friends. Not recommended for remote work because they dont have a WiFi facility  in 2026. Can you believe it?

text.text:
Service: Subpar (disappointing at times)
Food: Most of the items were good.
Overall experience: Average

Our family of five visited this restaurant hoping to enjoy a good meal and spend some quality time together. Unfortunately, the entire experience was ruined because of the poor service.

The main issue was with the person taking our order, Jeevan. We requested a lassi as soon as possible because my uncle was experiencing acid reflux and had a coughing fit. Instead of acknowledging the urgency or giving us an update, there was no response. Even after waiting nearly 15 minutes, every time we asked about it, we were either ignored or simply asked what else we wanted to order.

When we finally expressed our concern and asked when we could expect the lassi, his exact response was, "If you want, I can cancel the order," said in a very dismissive and arrogant manner. That level of customer service is unacceptable.

What made the experience even more uncomfortable was how he treated the rest of the staff. The employees serving the food were polite and trying their best, but he kept interrupting them, correcting them constantly, and creating confusion. At one point, he even yelled at another employee in front of us and other customers, warning him that it was "the last time" he was being warned. Watching an employee being publicly reprimanded like that was unprofessional and unpleasant. The staff appeared visibly anxious around him throughout our visit.

To make matters worse, the restaurant charged separately for the cover to carry the takeaway box, even though it was branded with the restaurant's own name. They also added a 5% service charge to the bill, marked as "voluntary," without asking whether we wanted to include it. None of these are legally okay. That practice felt misleading and unethical.

The food may have been decent, but the service completely overshadowed it. What should have been a pleasant family gathering turned into a frustrating experience. Sadly, we've lost interest in visiting this place again.

Amintiri is a standout destination for brunch enthusiasts, offering a refined yet cozy atmosphere that pairs perfectly with its artisanal menu. The cafe is widely praised for its consistent quality and sophisticated presentation, making it a favorite for both leisurely weekend breakfasts and quick, upscale coffee breaks.

* **Vanilla Cold Coffee:** This drink is a refreshing balance of smooth, premium coffee notes and a subtle, creamy vanilla finish, making it an ideal companion to their savory dishes.
* **Avo Toast:** Served on high-quality bread, the avocado toast is generously topped with fresh, seasoned mash and vibrant garnishes that provide a delightful crunch and tang.
* **Atmosphere:** Beyond the food, the cafe’s stylish interior and attentive service create a welcoming environment that feels like a true escape in the heart of the city.

Together, the fish curry and fish fry made for a complete and satisfying meal. The combination of bold, spicy gravy and crispy fried fish created a perfect harmony of textures and flavors, leaving a lasting impression.

text.text:
We finally made it for a Saturday lunch at this much-talked-about little eatery in Kammanahalli. Got there right at noon to be safe — a few tables still open, but the place was already humming with people settling into an early weekend meal.
The first thing that struck me was how unpretentious it all felt. Simple, neat, nothing overdone. The owner at the desk greeted us with a genuine smile — the kind that sets the tone before the food even arrives. The staff followed suit — warm, easy, and more than willing to guide us through the menu.
The food did take its time coming, which did catch us off guard for a place that clearly runs a full house most days. The famed Kerala meals weren’t available — apparently a cooking gas issue — which, oddly enough, just made us appreciate that we got anything at all without much fuss.
Now, the highlight — the seer fish mango curry. Quite honestly, the best I’ve had. And that includes some very reputed places back in Kerala. Beautifully balanced, sharp where it needed to be, and just... complete.
The crab fry and prawn masala, however, didn’t quite keep up. Both were decent, but hovered around the average mark — a bit of a surprise given how strong the meal had started.
The tender coconut pudding brought things right back on track. Light, just the right sweetness, with that gentle coconut finish — exactly what you want at the end of a meal like this.
Parotas were good. Ghee rice worked well too — no complaints there.
All in all, a solid 8 out of 10. And we’re not done here yet — feels like there’s more on that menu worth going back for.

text.text:
If you’re looking for a budget-friendly yet happening place in HSR Layout, Somaras Bar and Kitchen is definitely worth checking out. This place is quite popular among youngsters and working professionals, and it gets heavily crowded during peak hours, especially on weekends. So, if you want a good seat or a relaxed experience, making a reservation in advance is highly recommended.

The ambiance is one of the biggest highlights here—lively, energetic, and perfect for a fun evening with friends. We visited this place a few times with our group, and the vibe always felt fun and happening. Whether you’re planning a casual outing, a birthday celebration, or just a chill night out, the atmosphere fits all moods perfectly. The staff is well-trained, attentive, and manages the crowd efficiently, which is impressive considering how busy the place gets.

Coming to the food, it offers great value for money. The taste is satisfying across most dishes, and their bar snacks pair really well with the drinks. The menu also has a good variety of beers and cocktails, giving plenty of options to explore. One major advantage is the pricing—it is comparatively cheaper than many other bars and kitchens in HSR Layout, which makes it attractive for regular hangouts.

However, one concern we personally faced during multiple visits was related to hygiene and food quality consistency. A few times after dining here, some of us experienced stomach pain and health discomfort. We regularly visit many other places as well and did not face similar issues elsewhere. Because of this, we feel the management should pay more attention to maintaining hygiene standards and product quality. Affordable pricing is great, but quality and cleanliness should never be compromised.

Overall, Somaras Bar and Kitchen has an energetic crowd, good ambiance, and pocket-friendly pricing, but improving hygiene standards would make the experience much better and more reliable for customers.

text.text:
South Kitchen is one of those places that lives up to its reputation without trying too hard. The first thing you notice is the quick service—orders are prepared and served fast, and the self-service setup keeps everything moving smoothly even during busy hours.

The food is where it really stands out. The taste is consistently great, with that comforting, homely South Indian flavour that’s hard to get right everywhere. A big plus is that the menu is made without onion and garlic, which makes it a great option for Brahmins or anyone looking for sattvic-style food without compromising on taste.

The vibe adds to the experience. There’s a strong old Bengaluru charm here—the kind where people from all age groups come together, standing or sitting around, enjoying their food while conversations flow in the background. The constant chitter-chatter, the quick movement, and the no-frills setup all make it feel lively and authentic.

It’s not about fancy ambience or long, relaxed dining. It’s about good food, quick bites, and that familiar city feel that many places have lost over time. Despite the crowd, the system works efficiently, and you don’t feel overwhelmed.

Overall, South Kitchen is definitely worth the hype. It delivers on taste, speed, and simplicity, while also offering something unique with its no onion-garlic approach. A place you’ll keep going back to when you want something satisfying and fuss-free.

Visited Indian Biere House in JP Nagar with friends recently. Overall, it was a decent experience, though a bit mixed.

We tried the dumplings, sushi, veg pizza, and paneer bao buns. The dumplings and sushi were the highlights both tasted good, although the portions felt quite limited for the price (5 dumplings and 8 sushi pieces). The Mediterranean veg pizza was average and a bit too bready for my liking. I personally wouldn’t recommend the paneer bao buns as the sweet, spicy, and tangy combination didn’t work well for me.

We also tried their Kalajamun beer, sangria, and mimosa, but unfortunately none of the drinks really stood out.

Service was decent, and the ambience was pleasant enough, but considering the pricing, I do feel the portion sizes could be better. Overall, worth trying once for the dumplings and sushi, but there’s room for improvement in both quantity and consistency.

text.text:
Indian Bier House is a great place to visit, especially if you're looking for a vibrant dining experience with good food and an energetic crowd. The restaurant is extremely popular and tends to get packed during weekends, so be prepared for a bustling atmosphere. Despite the heavy footfall, the seating arrangement is well planned, allowing the space to feel organized even when it's full.

One aspect that stood out was the service. The staff were polite, attentive, and impressively efficient. Even during peak hours, they were quick to take orders and were accommodating when it came to food modifications or special requests. Their professionalism definitely enhanced the overall experience.

The ambience is lively and energetic, which many people may enjoy. However, it can get quite noisy, especially during busy hours. If you're planning to have a long conversation or a quiet catch-up with friends, you may find yourself raising your voice frequently just to be heard across the table.

Coming to the food, we tried the Veg OG Farmhouse Inspired Napoli-Style Pizza, which turned out to be quite enjoyable. The pizza had a flavorful combination of toppings and a well-made crust that complemented the ingredients nicely. It was satisfying without feeling overly heavy.

The Peri Peri Fries were easily one of the highlights of the meal. Crispy, generously seasoned, and packed with flavor, they were addictive and probably the standout dish we ordered.

We also tried the Veg Crystal Dimsums. While they were decent and well-presented, they didn't leave a lasting impression and felt average compared to the other dishes on the table.

text.text:
I have mixed feelings about my visit to Shift Lounge. There are some definite highlights, but the drink quality and service left a lot to be desired.

The Highlights: Food & Vibes
If you are coming here strictly for the food, you won't be disappointed.

Must-Try: The Fish Fingers are top-notch and easily the best thing on the menu.

Ambience: The overall vibe and decor are great, making it a visually pleasant spot to hang out.

The Lowlights: Drinks & Service
This is where the experience falls short.

The Bar: If you’re looking for quality drinks, this isn't the place. The alcohol felt very low quality; both the beer and the whiskey seemed diluted. Considering the high prices, the drink quality is a major letdown.

Service: The service is quite slow and feels a bit old-fashioned. You have to manually check the menu and flag down a waiter to get anything done.

Comfort: I wasn't a fan of the seating arrangements, and the air conditioning/ventilation could definitely use an upgrade.

Entertainment: The DJ was a miss for me. The track selection didn't really fit the mood or get the crowd grooving.

Summary: Go for the Fish Fingers and the atmosphere, but stick to bottled water or soda if you don't want to overpay for subpar drinks.

text.text:
We visited The Palms Brew & Kitchen for a team dinner, and it turned out to be a fantastic experience from start to finish.

The ambience is one of the biggest highlights—spacious, vibrant, and beautifully designed with plenty of seating options spread across two floors. There’s ample parking, which is a huge plus, especially for larger groups, and the large screens make it a great place to catch live sports while enjoying your meal.

The staff were warm, humble, and attentive throughout our visit. They patiently helped us with recommendations, making it easy to choose from the extensive menu.

We tried quite a few dishes, including Mutton Pepper, Dragon Chicken, Dumplings, Butter Garlic Prawns, Pizza, and Pasta, and every single dish was delicious. The portions were generous, the ingredients tasted fresh, and the flavours were perfectly balanced. Among the drinks, the Tongue Twister (non-alcoholic) was my personal favourite—refreshing and definitely worth trying.

Whether you’re planning a team outing, a family dinner, or a casual evening with friends, this place has something for everyone. The menu offers plenty of variety, the atmosphere is lively yet comfortable, and the overall experience is top-notch. I’d recommend reserving a table in advance if you’re visiting with a large group.

Overall, The Palms Brew & Kitchen delivers on every aspect—great ambience, delicious food, refreshing drinks, excellent service, and a wonderful vibe. Highly recommended, and I’ll definitely be visiting again!

Invoice Date: May 31, 2026
Cashier: S036
Invoice #: S03627T110007466
Having been to Starbucks locations all around the world, I was disappointed by the service here. First of all, I was never asked whether my order was for takeaway or dine-in. It was just served in a takeaway cup by default. I noticed this isn't just an isolated incident; many people in this cafe are being given takeaway cups by default. It seems to be a common practice here to just hand them out without asking, for which there is really no justification. My 10-year-old daughter always loves the presentation in the glass cups, so she completely missed out on that experience for her Tall Belgium Chocolate.
To make matters worse, because the chocolate was so thick and yummy, she couldn't easily sip it with a straw. When she went down to ask for a spoon, a staff member told her she should just use a straw and sent her away. When we adults went down to ask for a spoon ourselves, the employee actually responded by asking us "Why?". I have no clue if he even understands why a spoon is used, but we actually had to explain it to him before he finally changed his mind and gave us one. Is the staff just trying to avoid washing dishes, or is this an official Starbucks policy now?
Additionally, we also took a Starbucks reusable cup. The staff claimed they could not generate a bill for it due to a "technical issue," but they still collected ₹400 in cash from us without providing any receipt. This is highly unprofessional

text.text:
This Corner House  branch is comparatively more spacious than some of the older outlets, which makes the experience more comfortable.

The place is clean, well maintained, and has a simple self-service setup. Even when it gets crowded, things are managed smoothly. The ambience is casual and perfect for a quick dessert outing with friends or family.

Coming to the desserts, the highlight is obviously the Death by Chocolate (DBC), which remains unbeatable. Rich, indulgent, and full of chocolate layers — it’s a must-try every time. The hot chocolate fudge and cake fudge are also excellent options, especially if you want something similar at a slightly lower price. Flavours like rum & raisin, cashew fudge, almond fudge, and fruit-based sundaes are also very good, with a nice balance of taste and texture.

One thing I like is the consistency — the taste and quality remain the same across visits. Portions are satisfying, and the freshness is noticeable.

Prices are reasonable for the quality, though it can add up if you order multiple items.

Overall, one of the best places in Bangalore for ice cream and desserts. Simple, reliable, and always satisfying.

Food: 5/5
Service: 4/5
Atmosphere: 4/5
Value for Money: 4/5

text.text:
Corner House Ice Cream is not just an ice cream parlour — it’s a piece of my childhood and honestly, a whole emotion.

I’ve been coming here since I was little, and no matter how much Bangalore evolves, this place remains the OG dessert spot. They’re famous for their iconic sundaes, especially their signature ones — and rightfully so!

And that hot chocolate sauce? Absolutely to die for. Warm, rich, and poured so generously — it’s what makes every bite unforgettable.

My go-to order will always be the Cake Fudge (mini version of DBC) — because I don’t like sharing my ice cream 😌. It’s the perfect amount of indulgence, loaded with everything you need for a chocolate fix.

Honestly, no matter what mood I’m in — sad, happy, angry, or celebrating — there’s only one solution:
Corner House’s Cake Fudge.

Some places serve desserts, but this one serves comfort, nostalgia, and happiness in every bite 🤍✨

text.text:
I have been a regular customer at Albek , RT Nagar, for the last 5–6 years, but my recent experiences have been extremely disappointing.

About two weeks ago, I ordered tandoori chicken and found multiple chicken feathers in it. When I brought it to the staff’s attention, they initially said it was “common” and suggested I simply remove the feathers and continue eating. Only after I insisted on speaking to the manager did they apologize.

The person at the billing counter explained that all the food is prepared at their main kitchen in Rajajinagar and that the RT Nagar outlet only cooks and serves it. He assured me that he would escalate my complaint to the main Rajajinagar team and apologized for the experience. Since I had been a loyal customer for years, I decided to let it go, assuming it was a one-time issue and that the problem would be addressed.

Unfortunately, when I visited again yesterday for dinner, I experienced the exact same issue. I found a chicken feather in my chicken biryani. We also ordered the Andhra Kebab, which was equally disappointing and nowhere close to the quality the restaurant was once known for.

This time, I didn’t even bother complaining because I had already raised the issue during my previous visit and was assured it would be taken seriously. I simply paid my bill and left. When the staff asked why I was leaving disappointed, I told them that the same hygiene issue had happened again.

While I was leaving, I also noticed two other customers returning their food to the staff because they were unhappy with it. I don’t know the exact reason for their complaints, but it reinforced my impression that the overall quality has declined.

It is very disappointing that despite assuring me the complaint had been escalated to the main kitchen in Rajajinagar, nothing seems to have changed. Finding chicken feathers in food once is unacceptable. Finding them repeatedly over multiple visits points to a serious lack of hygiene and quality control.

As someone who has been visiting AlBek for over five years, it’s sad to see such a decline in standards over the past few months. I can no longer recommend this place. If hygiene and food quality are important to you, I would advise avoiding this restaurant until these issues are properly addressed.
